title: claude-commands skill is unloadable: its documented bang-syntax executes at load time
description: Invoking the claude-code:claude-commands skill fails outright with: Shell command failed for pattern (backtick-cat placeholder): cat: path/to/file: No such file or directory. Reproduced twice by an independent agent and once directly. Cause: SKILL.md line 90 documents the command file-inclusion placeholder using the literal bang-backtick-cat form as an inline code span. Claude Code expands that pattern when loading the file, so documenting the syntax executes it. The skill that teaches command authoring is broken by the exact feature it teaches. Impact: this is a published marketplace plugin, so every user who installs claude-code gets a skill that errors on load rather than loading; and any agent instructed to load it, including our own plugin-work prompts that name it, silently loses that context. Nothing in test/validate-skills-quality.nu catches this — the 17 per-skill checks validate structure and references but never attempt to LOAD a skill, so a skill can be unloadable while scoring 17/17. Two parts to resolve: escape or restructure the placeholder so it documents without executing (verify by actually loading the skill afterward, not by reading it), and sweep every skill, command, hook and agent file for other executable bang-backtick patterns that would fire on load. Consider whether a load-time smoke check belongs in the validator, since structural validity currently implies nothing about loadability. Broader note worth capturing: skill bodies can execute shell at load time, which is a security property, not just a correctness one. Found while planning the pointer-validation gap closure.
close_reason: PR #163: skill loads again; KEY= marker for bang triggers, backslash for $ARGUMENTS, bare names for CLAUDE_* since the braced form ignores the escape. Verified by loading, cache restored byte-identical.

comments.text:
Sweep result: three other files carry the same executable pattern, and the distinction between them and the broken one is instructive.

Sites found: claude-skills/SKILL.md:162, claude-skills/references/frontmatter-fields.md:70, claude-commands/references/examples.md:76 (plus :67 as an inline span). All four use git diff HEAD.

The failing instance in claude-commands/SKILL.md:90 is an INLINE code span inside a sentence, wrapped in double backticks. It fails because cat path/to/file exits non-zero. The other three sit inside fenced markdown blocks AND their command (git diff HEAD) exits zero.

So two variables differ at once and observation alone cannot separate them: we cannot tell whether fenced blocks protect the pattern, or whether those three execute harmlessly on every load and nobody noticed. claude-skills loads successfully today either way.

That matters for the fix. If fences do not protect, then loading claude-skills silently shells out to git on every load, which is a side effect nobody asked for and would misbehave outside a git repo. Determine which it is empirically before choosing an escaping approach, and do not assume the fenced sites are safe just because they load.

Corrected framing for this bug: the failure is not that a skill documents the syntax, it is that a skill documented it with a command that fails. A skill that documents it with a command that succeeds has the same defect and no symptom.

DEFINITIVE: fenced blocks DO execute, and the corruption is broader than shell injection.

Verified by loading claude-code:claude-skills directly and reading what arrived. Its Dynamic context and substitutions section is supposed to teach the syntax. What loaded instead:

- The fenced example block, nested inside a five-backtick outer fence, arrived as executed OUTPUT: a bash-completed-with-no-output marker, then a node version string, then an npm version string. The syntax being taught is gone from the rendered content.
- Every documented substitution placeholder was also expanded: the arguments placeholder rendered empty, the indexed-argument form was mangled, the session-id placeholder rendered as the live session uuid, the effort placeholder rendered as the current effort level, and the skill-directory placeholder rendered as an absolute plugin-cache path.

So the earlier open question is settled: outer fencing does NOT protect, and the three sites previously called safe are live executions on every load. They differ from the broken one only in that their command exits zero.

This widens the bug in three ways:
1. Scope is not just bang-backtick shell injection. All runtime substitutions expand in skill bodies, so any skill documenting placeholder syntax silently corrupts its own teaching content.
2. Severity for the loadable sites is not cosmetic. A reader learning the feature is shown output where the syntax should be, which is worse than an error because it fails silently and looks plausible.
3. The session-id expansion means loading a skill can inject live session identifiers into content. Minor here, but it is a disclosure surface worth noting given this repo publishes to a public marketplace.

Fix direction: documenting this syntax requires an escaping form that survives load. Determine empirically which forms survive, since backticks and outer fences both demonstrably do not. Prose description without literal syntax does survive, and claude-skills already uses that approach for the inline form in the sentence immediately above the broken block. Verify any fix by loading the skill and reading what arrives, never by reading the source.

Also note the loaded copy came from the plugin cache, so a repo-side fix needs a cache refresh before re-verification.

Experimental results: what escaping actually works.

Method: backed up the plugin-cache copy of the skill, applied one candidate at a time, invoked the skill, observed. Cache restored byte-identical afterward and verified with diff.

CANDIDATE THAT FAILED. Removing the space between the opening double-backtick and the bang does NOT neutralize it. The skill still failed to load with the same cat error. Conclusion: markdown code-span delimiters are stripped before the injection scan runs, so the bang still lands at position zero of the scanned text and reads as line-start. This matters because it means you cannot reason about safety from the markdown source shape.

FORM THAT IS PROVEN SAFE. A non-whitespace character immediately before the bang, in the RENDERED text. Evidence is already in the file: line 88 contains the KEY-equals form as an inline example, and its command never executes, otherwise loading would fail on a command-not-found for that placeholder rather than on the cat. So the skill already contains a working demonstration of its own escape, one line above the site that breaks it.

FORMS PROVEN UNSAFE, all previously observed: bang at line start inside a fenced block; the same inside a five-backtick outer fence; and an inline code span with a leading space. Fencing of any depth does not protect.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE DOC RULE. The skill states the inline bang is recognized only at line start or immediately after whitespace. The first candidate result shows that rule is misleading as written, because delimiter stripping can turn a mid-line position into a line-start one. The rule needs restating in terms of the scanned text rather than the source text.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIX. There is no way to display the literal syntax at the start of a line. Any site that shows it must place a visible non-whitespace character immediately before the bang and tell the reader to drop that character. That is clunky but it is the only shape that both displays the syntax and survives loading. Do not use invisible characters for this: a zero-width escape that a reader cannot see produces copy-paste that silently does not work.

VERIFICATION PATH for whoever implements. Fix the repo files, copy the fixed file over its plugin-cache counterpart, invoke the skill, and read what arrives. Reading the source proves nothing here. Restore the cache from a backup afterward and diff to confirm.

title: Skills instruct agents to run scripts that do not exist
description:
Same defect class as claude-skills-126 (documented artifact absent) but for EXECUTABLES, so the failure is an agent running a command that cannot work. Verified with ls.

1. plugins/tools/github/skills/act/SKILL.md:635 states 'The plugin includes an installation script at scripts/install-act.sh', and :660-661 instruct 'chmod +x scripts/install-act.sh' then './scripts/install-act.sh'. The directory contains ONLY install-act.nu. Fix: point at install-act.nu and correct the invocation to nu (this repo's convention is nushell, so the .nu file is the right artifact and the .sh reference is the error). Clears the github/act:links waiver.

2. plugins/tools/agent-sandboxing/skills/sandbox/SKILL.md:89 states 'scripts/render-claim.nu, scripts/wait-bound.nu, scripts/list-claims.nu — nushell scripts invoked by the slash commands.' The skill has NO scripts/ directory at all. Either the three scripts were never written (then the slash commands that invoke them are also broken — check them) or they live elsewhere and the paths are wrong. Resolve which, then fix or delete the claim.

NOT a defect, checked and cleared: plugins/tools/proxmox/skills/proxmox/SKILL.md:31,:43,:66 mention scripts/proxmox.nu and scripts/golden-image.nu, but line 66 makes explicit these are existing scripts at ~/github/infra/scripts/ — an external operator repo, not bundled artifacts. Worth disambiguating the bare 'scripts/' shorthand so it does not read as a bundled path, but nothing is missing.

Also confirmed illustrative, not defects: scripts/foo.sh (claude-skills:172, explicitly a placeholder for CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR usage), scripts/deploy.sh (claude-commands:403, inside the fabricated-syntax block already covered by 126), and the generic install.sh / uninstall.sh / validate.sh / process.sh names in teaching contexts.

Lesson for the links check (claude-skills-132): it cannot distinguish a bundled-artifact claim from an illustrative path, which is why both a real bug and a placeholder land in the same waiver. Any fix needs that distinction, otherwise it gets waived as noise again.
close_reason: github/act now points at scripts/install-act.nu with the real nu invocation. agent-sandboxing item was a false positive on my part — scripts exist at the plugin root and commands invoke them correctly via CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT; the SKILL.md notation was ambiguous and is now explicit.

comments.text:
CORRECTION — item 2 of this issue was WRONG, and the error was mine.

I claimed agent-sandboxing/skills/sandbox/SKILL.md:89 named three scripts that do not exist, and speculated the slash commands invoking them were broken too. Both false. Verified:
- The three scripts DO exist at the plugin root: plugins/tools/agent-sandboxing/scripts/{render-claim.nu, wait-bound.nu, list-claims.nu}.
- The commands invoke them correctly: provision.md:38 and :50, status.md:19 and :46 all use 'nu ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/render-claim.nu'. mise.toml tasks wire them too. Nothing was broken.
- The only real defect was ambiguous notation in the SKILL.md bullet, which read as skill-relative. Fixed to name ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ explicitly and state that the scripts live at the plugin root.

Item 1 (github/act) was correct and is fixed: the SKILL.md referenced scripts/install-act.sh with a chmod+execute instruction while only install-act.nu exists. Now points at 'nu scripts/install-act.nu', with the described behaviour read from the actual script rather than assumed.

ROOT CAUSE of my false positive, which matters for claude-skills-132 item 5 and claude-skills-135: my dangling-path sweep resolved every 'scripts/...' and 'references/...' mention relative to the SKILL.md's own directory. Plugin-root-relative and repo-root-relative citations are legitimate and common, so any real links check must attempt skill-dir, plugin-root, and repo-root resolution before reporting a dangling pointer. A checker that only tries one of the three manufactures false positives — which is how a real bug ends up dismissed alongside noise.

title: claude-commands skill documents a slash-command syntax that does not exist
description:
VERIFIED: plugins/tools/claude-code/skills/claude-commands/SKILL.md teaches a Handlebars-style templating language Claude Code slash commands do not support. Anyone following this skill writes broken commands.

Evidence (measured, not inferred):
- 43 occurrences of {{...}} in the SKILL.md: {{arg}}/{{arg1}}/{{environment}} substitution (lines 75, 85-87, 97-102), {{#if}}/{{else}}/{{/if}}/{{#unless}} conditionals (116-123, 187-194, 384-392), {{shell:...}} and {{file:...}} inclusion (135-139, 150, 177, 261, 275), and HTML-comment metadata blocks instead of YAML frontmatter (57-59, 200-206).
- ZERO occurrences of the real syntax in that file: no $ARGUMENTS, no $1-$9, no argument-hint, no @file.
- This repo's OWN shipped commands use the real syntax: plugins/core/commands/work.md and restraint-audit.md both use $ARGUMENTS with YAML frontmatter carrying description and argument-hint.

Actual syntax to document (verify against https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slash-commands before writing): $ARGUMENTS for all args, $1-$9 positional, ! prefix in backticks for shell pre-execution, @ for file references, YAML frontmatter fields description / argument-hint / allowed-tools / model / disable-model-invocation.

Also: dead example URL at line 410 (github.com/anthropics/claude-code/tree/main/examples/commands).

Rewrite, do not reorganize — moving fabricated content into references/ just files the fabrication. Salvageable: file locations and kebab naming (28-40), namespaced command directories (237-250), plugin.json wiring (211-235), security principles (369-377).

Target shape: body = frontmatter field table + argument/shell/file semantics + locations and namespacing (~150 lines); references/examples.md = two or three real worked commands in real syntax.

Note the claude-code/claude-commands:anti_fab waiver in test/quality-baseline.json hid this twice: no anti-fabrication section, and fabricated content. Remove the waiver when fixed (the ratchet is shrink-only).

Found during the Claude-5 context-engineering audit of the claude-code plugin.
close_reason: Rewritten from the official docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/slash-commands, which now serves the merged skills page). 410 lines of fabricated Handlebars syntax replaced with a 119-line body plus 93-line references/examples.md. Zero {{ }} remain; 8 $ARGUMENTS. anti_fab waiver removed from the ratchet.

comments.text:
Precision correction on the evidence: 43 LINES contain {{, and 51 total {{ occurrences (grep -c counts lines, grep -o counts occurrences). The original description said 43 occurrences. The defect is unchanged; the count was imprecise.

A repo-wide sweep also confirms claude-commands is the only genuine case. github/skills/workflows has 49 bare {{ of which 48 are real GitHub Actions dollar-brace expressions, and the ansible, dagu, slidev, and mise hits are legitimate Jinja2, Vue, and mise templating. claude-commands has 51 bare {{ and zero dollar-brace, which isolates it. Any syntax-vs-usage CI check (claude-skills-132 item 5) must compare against the real syntax for the format in question rather than grepping for double-brace blindly.

title: chore(security): public-repo disclosure lint — block real op:// vault paths, RFC1918 IPs, estate hostnames
description:
A security incident (PR #123) revealed that real infrastructure identifiers were inadvertently published to this public repository: valid op:// vault paths with private vault names, RFC1918 IP literals identifying infrastructure nodes, and estate hostnames. These leaked via the exported .bees/issues.jsonl after merging the proxmox skill PR.

Add a repo lint to CI that fails when content under plugins/ contains:
1. op:// references with non-placeholder vault names (allowlist placeholder names only: <vault>, your-vault, Vault, any arbitrary text that is NOT an actual vault name)
2. RFC1918 IP literals (10.x.x.x, 172.16-31.x.x, 192.168.x.x)
3. Known estate hostnames (pve, pve2, etc.)

Implement via:
- gitleaks custom rules (add to .gitleaks.toml or validate task) to fail CI on these patterns
- or a dedicated skill-authoring validation task
- Update CLAUDE.md + claude-skills skill-authoring docs with the lint checklist

This ensures future exports of .bees/issues.jsonl stay clean and reduce risk of infrastructure reconnaissance leaks.
close_reason: disclosure lint shipped in PR #125 — test/validate-disclosure.nu wired into mise test + CI, docs in CLAUDE.md and claude-skills skill

title: Add bundles pack and import commands to runex skill bundles.nu
description:
The runex skill's bundles.nu has list/show/validate but no pack or import commands. The Runex API has POST /api/bundles/import accepting multipart tar.gz uploads (BundleController.import_bundle at lib/runex_web/controllers/api/bundle_controller.ex:8). We need:

1. bundles.nu pack <bundle-dir> — creates a tar.gz archive from a bundle directory. Output to stdout path or --output flag. Uses 'tar -czf' under the hood.
2. bundles.nu import <archive-path> --host <runex-url> — POSTs the tar.gz to the target Runex's /api/bundles/import endpoint as multipart form upload. Returns the import result.

These are needed for vantageex-219 (pack VantageEx bundles and import to Mini's Runex) and for the bundle versioning epic (vantageex-218).

title: fix: /core:security hook uses relative path — check-secrets-before-commit.sh fails on every Bash call
description:
The /core:security skill's SKILL.md frontmatter defines a PreToolUse:Bash hook with a relative command path:

  command: "./hooks/check-secrets-before-commit.sh"

This resolves from the user's current working directory (e.g. ~/github/vantageex), not from the skill's own directory. The script only exists at the skill's hooks/ directory. Result: every Bash tool call produces 5+ non-blocking errors:

  PreToolUse:Bash hook error
  Failed with non-blocking status code: /bin/sh: ./hooks/check-secrets-before-commit.sh: No such file or directory

Fix: change the command to use the CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT variable (same pattern the security-guidance and hookify plugins use):

  command: "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/check-secrets-before-commit.sh"

File: plugins/core/skills/security/SKILL.md (frontmatter hooks section, around line 10)
Also verify the script exists at: plugins/core/skills/security/hooks/check-secrets-before-commit.sh

One-line fix. Bump the plugin version in plugin.json after.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #52

- Hook command uses absolute path via CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT
- Loading /core:security skill no longer produces hook errors on Bash calls
- The gitleaks scan still runs correctly when the hook fires (test by running a Bash command after loading the skill)

title: Document the verify-by-loading loop; plugin content is snapshotted per session
description: Skill bodies are preprocessed before the model sees them, so shell-injection patterns run and substitution placeholders expand. Reading the source therefore proves nothing about what a reader actually receives, and two bugs this session, claude-skills-169 and 172, were only provable by loading. Nothing in our skills tells an author this, and the verification loop has a trap that silently defeats it. The trap: invoking any skill from a plugin appears to snapshot that whole plugin content for the session, so later edits are never re-read. A worker spent a long stretch iterating on candidate fixes and got the identical stale error every time, and only caught it by injecting a unique marker into an untouched skill and finding it absent from a fresh invocation. Because the mandatory session-start skill list already touches the claude-code plugin, anyone fixing a skill there hits this immediately. The escape hatch is the reload-plugins command, which only the operator can run. The loop that works: fix the repo file, copy it over its counterpart in the plugin cache under the account and plugin and active version, checking installed_plugins for the active version since stale version directories linger, ask the operator to reload plugins, invoke the skill and read what arrives, then restore the cache from backup and diff to prove byte-identical restoration. Never leave an operator cache modified. Also worth recording alongside it: the established escaping facts, which are that a visible non-whitespace character before the bang protects it, fencing does not protect at any nesting depth, code-span delimiters are stripped before the scan so removing a space does not help, the backslash escape works on the bare dollar-name form but not the braced form, and invisible characters must never be used as escapes because readers copy-paste something that silently fails. Home for this is the claude-skills skill, which already documents dynamic context and substitutions and is where an author would look. Verify any edit to that section by loading it, since the section documents the very syntax that expands.

title: CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT expands in skill bodies, corrupting the docs that teach it
description: The brace-expansion token for the plugin root expands at skill load time in skill BODIES, not only in manifests. This was assumed out of scope during PR 163 on the grounds that it is a manifest-time mechanism; that judgment is disproven by direct observation. Loading the claude-hooks skill returns every occurrence in its body already replaced by the absolute cache path. Two self-defeating examples from the arrived content: a table row explaining the token as the absolute path to the plugin root arrives as the literal path followed by that explanation, and a best-practice bullet reading Use the token, never hardcode plugin paths arrives with the token replaced by a hardcoded path, instructing the reader to do the opposite of what it says. Affected skill bodies on main: claude-hooks SKILL.md with nine sites, claude-plugins SKILL.md with six, plugin-marketplace SKILL.md with about fifteen plus seven more in its schema-specification reference, agent-sandboxing sandbox SKILL.md around line 89, and core security SKILL.md around line 10. Genuinely out of scope and to be left alone: occurrences in hooks.json, plugin.json, and command bodies where expansion is the desired behavior. Two harms. First, silent teaching corruption, the same class rated worse than an error on claude-skills-169, because the page still reads plausibly while telling the reader the wrong thing. Second, minor disclosure, since the expansion injects a local absolute path including the account name into loaded content, matching the concern already recorded for session identifiers. Fix approach: apply the convention established by PR 163, which is a visible marker the reader is told to drop, since no escape survives loading for the braced form. Verify by loading each affected skill and reading what arrives, never by reading the source, and note that a plugin reload is required between editing and verifying. Found during the Gate 3 review of PR 163.
close_reason: PR #164: three-way fix — copyable examples to references/, prose to bare names, 13 functional invocations left braced. Load-verified on claude-hooks.

comments.text:
Independently reproduced, with two corrections to the original scope and one new constraint that shapes the fix.

CONFIRMED by loading claude-hooks directly. The self-defeating bullet arrives with the token replaced by an absolute cache path, so the rendered line instructs the reader to hardcode the path in the same breath as telling them never to hardcode plugin paths. The explanatory bullet describing the token as the plugin root expanded at runtime arrives as the expanded path followed by that description, which reads as nonsense.

CORRECTION 1, scope is smaller than filed. The core security skill is NOT affected. Its occurrence is in frontmatter, inside the hooks block, where the token is functional and correct. Frontmatter is not delivered on load, which is why loading that skill shows no expansion anywhere. Real scope is 41 body occurrences across five files: claude-hooks 8, claude-plugins 6, plugin-marketplace 18, its schema-specification reference 8, and agent-sandboxing sandbox 1. Verified by splitting each file at its frontmatter delimiter and counting body versus frontmatter separately.

CORRECTION 2, and this is the significant one. Fenced code blocks do NOT protect substitution. I had hoped only the prose sites were affected, which would have cut the fix from 41 sites to about 7. They are not. The JSON examples inside triple-backtick fences arrive with the token already replaced by the absolute path, so every hooks.json example in the hooks skill currently teaches an agent to write a hardcoded path. This matches the earlier finding that fences do not protect bang execution either.

NEW CONSTRAINT the fix must solve. These sites are unlike the ones fixed in PR 163. There the literal syntax was being displayed for a reader to understand. Here the JSON blocks are meant to be COPIED into a real hooks.json, where the token must survive verbatim. A visible drop-this marker of the kind used for the bang trigger would be copied along with the rest of the block and produce a broken config, so the marker approach cannot be applied unchanged. Worse, the practical consumer is usually an agent reading the skill and then writing the JSON itself, so whatever the example shows is what gets written.

No escape is known to work. The leading backslash does not escape the braced form, proven on claude-skills-169. A preceding visible character does not help either, since the braced substitution has no line-start or whitespace rule to defeat, unlike the bang trigger. Any alteration that breaks the literal also changes what a copier ends up with.

That means the fix is a design decision rather than a mechanical substitution, and needs a plan and a review before implementation. Candidate directions worth weighing: relocate copyable examples into templates, which are assets and are not loaded into context, leaving the body to describe and point at them; or keep examples in the body with an unmistakable marker plus a per-block warning; or describe the token in prose and stop showing complete copyable blocks in the body. Each trades teaching quality against copy correctness differently.

title: elixir/testing has no test-isolation section, but a reference cites one

title: Verify or retire the host.docker.internal claim in the container skill

title: No check validates links in agent files, and two danglers proved it
description:
Gate 3 on PR #155 found the same defect class twice in one PR, both invisible to CI because check 14 (links) parses SKILL.md content only — validate-skills-quality.nu:1674 operates on the stripped SKILL.md, never on agents/*.md or commands/*.md.

Instance 1, PRE-EXISTING: plugins/core/skills/bees/agents/bees-worker.md:151 said 'consult references/skill-catalog.md' relative to the bees skill, where that file did not exist. Dangling for as long as it had been written; found only because the beads restructure forced someone to look. Fixed in #155 by moving the catalog into bees.

Instance 2, INTRODUCED BY #155 AND CAUGHT IN REVIEW: plugins/core/agents/setup.md:172 said 'Use the beads-worker agent', which core stopped shipping when beads moved to its own plugin. Namespaced greps (core:beads, tools:beads) could not see it because setup names the agent bare. Fixed in the same PR.

Two instances in one PR is the argument: agent and command files carry pointers to references, agents, and skills, and nothing checks any of them. A skill file gets links validated; an agent file that says the same thing does not.

Proposed: extend the links check to agents/*.md and commands/*.md. Considerations — (a) agent files legitimately name agents rather than paths ('the beads-worker agent'), so a path-only check misses instance 2; catching that class needs agent-NAME resolution against the plugin's registered agents, which is closer to the invocations check than to links; (b) cross-plugin pointers are now legitimate (see the cross-skill-qualified exemption), so the check must honour the same escape hatch; (c) expect pre-existing failures — baseline them per the ratchet rather than blocking.

Related: claude-skills-141 built the syntax-vs-usage check for a similar 'documented thing does not exist' class, but scoped to slash commands, agent frontmatter, and hook events — not to prose pointers inside agent bodies.

title: /core:bees documents a `bees update --labels` flag that does not exist in bees 0.4.0
description:
## Objective
Correct the /core:bees skill so its label guidance matches the installed bees CLI.

## Evidence (verified 2026-07-28)
`bees --version` -> bees 0.4.0
`bees update --help` -> flags are: --title, -s/--status, -p/--priority, -a/--assignee,
  -d/--description, -t/--type, -o/--owner, --design, --acceptance, --notes, --external-ref,
  --due, --defer, --json
There is NO `--labels` flag on `bees update`.

The /core:bees skill states, in its "Priorities and Labels" / complexity-labels guidance:
  "Apply with `bees update <id> --labels \"...\"`, not `bees label add` — only `bees update --labels`
   keeps the priority field synced with the `priority:pN` label."

That command is unrunnable on 0.4.0. Agents instructed to follow it either error out or silently
fall back to `bees label add`.

## Observed impact
Nine bees were filed on 2026-07-28 (github-644/645/646/647, vantageex-697/698/699/700/701) by
agents that had been told to use `bees update --labels`. All fell back to `bees label add`. All nine
were then verified to have priority FIELD and `priority:pN` label IN SYNC, and `bees ready` sorts
P1 first correctly in both trackers. So on 0.4.0 the sync happens by some other path — the skill's
stated rationale for preferring `update --labels` does not hold either.

Net: no data was corrupted, but the skill instructs an impossible command and gives a false reason
for it. Every agent prompt that quotes this guidance propagates an unfollowable instruction.

## Acceptance criteria
- Determine how label/priority sync ACTUALLY works in bees 0.4.0 — verify empirically, do not assume.
  Specifically: does `bees label add priority:p1` set the priority field? Does `bees update -p 1`
  add the label? Test both directions on a scratch bee and record the results.
- Rewrite the /core:bees guidance to name commands that exist, with the real sync semantics.
- If a `--labels` flag is genuinely wanted, file a separate upstream issue against
  https://github.com/ctxshift/bees rather than documenting it as though it ships.
- Check the rest of /core:bees against the 0.4.0 CLI for other drift of the same kind (verify every
  command the skill names actually exists and takes the flags shown) and fix what you find.

## Deliverables
- Corrected /core:bees skill
- A short note in the skill recording the bees version its guidance was verified against, so the
  next drift is detectable
close_reason:
ALREADY FIXED — this describes a defect corrected earlier the same day in PR #151 (claude-skills-157/158), which merged before this issue was filed.

Current state on main, plugins/core/skills/bees/SKILL.md:254: 'Apply with `bees label add <id> <label>`, one label per invocation — `bees update` has no `--labels` flag, and a comma-separated string becomes a single literal label. Adding a `priority:pN` label does not change the issue's priority field; set that separately with `bees update <id> -p <N>`.' A repo-wide grep for 'update.*--labels' returns nothing in the bees skill.

The evidence in this issue is correct about the binary — bees 0.4.0 genuinely has no --labels on update — it is the claim about what the SKILL says that is stale. #151 corrected twelve documented behaviours in that skill against the binary, this being one of them, and also measured that 'bees label add <id> "a,b"' creates ONE literal label (verified via --json returning ["a,b"] versus ["a","b"] when added separately).

Filed at 13:19:04Z, apparently from a scratchpad clone or context predating the #151 merge. No action needed. If a future agent re-files this, check main before filing — the corrected text names the nonexistent flag explicitly, which reads like the defect if skimmed.

comments.text:
EMPIRICAL FINDING 2026-07-28 — answers this bee'\''s main acceptance criterion.

Tested directly on bees 0.4.0 against a real issue (vantageex-708):
- `bees label add <id> priority:p3` adds the LABEL only. The priority FIELD stayed at its default of 2. Verified via `bees show <id> --json | jq .priority` → 2 while labels contained priority:p3.
- `bees update <id> -p 3` sets the FIELD. After it: priority_field=3, labels=priority:p3 — in sync.

So the two are independent, and `bees ready` orders on the FIELD. Setting only the label silently mis-sorts the queue.

Correct guidance for /core:bees on 0.4.0:
  bees update <id> -p N          # sets the priority field (what bees ready sorts on)
  bees label add <id> priority:pN # adds the label (for filtering/display)
  Do BOTH when you want them consistent.

This also corrects an earlier verification in this same session that reported nine bees as "all synced" after `bees label add` — that was coincidence: those bees were P1/P2 and 2 is the default, so field and label happened to agree. It is not evidence that label add syncs.

The skill'\''s current text (`bees update <id> --labels "..."`, described as the way to keep priority synced) is wrong twice over: the flag does not exist, and its stated rationale does not describe how sync actually works.

title: bees skill's mise.toml template ships broken create flags
description:
Found by Gate 3 on PR #150 and confirmed by a follow-up grep. plugins/core/skills/bees/templates/mise.toml declares a bees:create task with '--labels (-l)' (line 70) and '--parent (-p)' (line 73), and forwards them to the binary as '-l' (line 80) and '-p'. Measured against bees 0.4.0: 'bees create' has NO label flag ('bees create x -l bug' -> Invalid argument '-l', exit 1) and NO parent flag; '-p' is '--priority <N>' (1=critical..4=low), so a parent id passed through -p is either rejected or silently misread as a priority.

This template is shipped for users to copy into their own mise.toml, and PR #150's new install stub in SKILL.md points readers directly at it — so the broken task is now more discoverable, not less.

Also from the same review, likely the same audit: 'bees list --labels a --json' returned EMPTY for an issue verifiably carrying label 'a' (open, labels ["a","b","priority:p1"]). mise.toml:147/154 declares and forwards that same --labels filter, and references/commands.md:36 documents it. If the filter genuinely does not work, three places document a no-op.

Fix: correct the create task to use -t/--type and -p/--priority per the real flag list, add labels via a follow-up 'bees label add' call (one per label — a comma string becomes one literal label), and verify the list/ready/prime --labels filters against the binary before keeping them.

Related: claude-skills-157 audits references/commands.md against the binary. This issue is the template + filter half; keep them separate so neither blocks the other.
close_reason:
Shipped as PR #151 alongside claude-skills-157 — same verification setup, so they were done together. The bees mise template's bees:create forwarded -l (create has NO label flag; errors exit 1) and -p as a parent id (-p is --priority <N>, so a parent id was either rejected or silently misread as a priority). Gate 3 confirmed both, plus three more broken tasks the original issue did not name: bees:prime forwarded --status/--labels to a command that takes zero flags, bees:config's no-arg branch called a bare bees config that errors, and bees:label:add/remove advertised comma-separated labels that the binary stores as one literal label.

Critically, the same broken tasks existed in this repo's OWN root mise.toml, not just the shipped template — found only because the grep was widened to repo-wide. Both copies are now corrected and byte-identical in their bees:* sections, and a bees:import task was added so the migration table's beads:rebuild -> bees:import mapping resolves to something real. Corrected task bodies were executed, not just read.

title: Audit bees commands.md against the installed binary end to end
description:
Found while implementing the claude-skills-143 first slice. The bees Commands Reference documented several things the installed binary does not do, and only the ones directly in the way were verified and fixed in PR #150. The rest of the file has NOT been checked command by command.

Verified WRONG and fixed in #150: 'bees update <id> --labels' (no such flag; bees label add is the path) in SKILL.md; 'bees create "Title" -l "bug,priority:high"' (create has NO label flag at all — errors 'Invalid argument -l', exit 1); 'bees create "Title" -p <parent-id>' (-p is --priority <N>, not parent; create has no parent flag); 'bees label add <id> "bug,priority:high"' (creates ONE literal label — bees show --json returns ["bug,priority:high"] versus ["bug","priority:high"] when added separately; the plain-text rendering hides this, showing 'bug,priority:high' vs 'bug, priority:high' differing only by a space).

Also measured: adding a priority:pN label does NOT change the issue's priority field; that needs bees update <id> -p <N>.

The remaining subcommands in references/commands.md (list, show, update, close, ready, dep, comment, config, sync, prime) were moved byte-faithfully and never validated against the binary. Audit each flag and example by running it, and correct or delete what does not hold.

Worth noting for tooling: this is exactly the defect class claude-skills-141's syntax-vs-usage check was built for, but that check covers slash commands, agent frontmatter, and hook events — not CLI flags cited inside skill bodies. A skill documenting a tool's CLI has no ground truth in this repo to diff against, only the binary. If this audit finds many more, consider whether a check can shell out to --help for tools the repo actually installs via mise.
close_reason:
Shipped as PR #151, together with claude-skills-158. Twelve documented behaviours corrected against bees 0.4.0 in a MANDATORY skill loaded by every agent at every tier. Every corrected command was executed and its output pasted; Gate 3 independently re-verified each NEW claim, because the failure mode of a truth-up is replacing false claims with different false ones.

THREE BEHAVIOURAL CLAIMS WERE FALSE, and these matter more than the flag typos because a wrong flag fails loudly while a wrong behavioural claim gets believed:
- bees prime returns NO issue data. It was documented as "a formatted markdown summary of issues" listing titles, descriptions, labels, dependencies and status. It emits 58 lines of static agent-workflow cheatsheet; a repo with 4 issues produced zero issue-id mentions. That was the skill's headline AI-integration feature, wrong in about six places. Issue context comes from bees list --json / bees show --json.
- bees ready does not consider parent state. Documented as requiring parent issues to still be open; a child stays ready with its parent open AND after it closes. parent-child and related deps never gate readiness in either direction. The corrected text adds the remedy: add an explicit blocks edge, verified to work.
- No .beads symlink exists. bees init creates only .bees/, and the binary REMOVES legacy symlinks. Claimed in five SKILL.md sites plus installation.md and sources.md — and used by plugins/pm/spec-harvest as a DETECTION HEURISTIC for "is this a bees repo", which misclassified every bees repo.

NINE SYNTAX DEFECTS: list --labels and ready --labels do not exist (exit 1, not a silent no-op); bare bees config errors requiring a subcommand; prime takes zero flags; "all 12 subcommands" undercounts 19; the migration script passed -l to create; and four mise tasks forwarded flags the binary rejects.

SCOPE GREW 7 FILES TO 12, CORRECTLY. The repo-wide grep found the same broken forwarding in this repo's OWN root mise.toml (main lines 688, 691, 765, 788), so `mise run bees:create --labels ...` had been failing here, not only in the template shipped to users.

THE PROCESS LESSON, third round running: each round's grep rule was right but scoped one level too small. #150 said "grep body + all references" — that scope let the symlink claim survive in installation.md, a file #150 ITSELF created by moving the VS Code section. #151 widened it to repo-wide and immediately found two more sites. Scope the grep to the repo, not to the files you planned to touch.

Follow-ups filed: claude-skills-159 (bees silently accepts invalid enum values — a typo'd status removes an issue from the ready queue with no signal) and claude-skills-160 (two pm agent files still imply prime returns issue data).

title: Syntax-vs-usage cross-check: detect documented syntax that does not exist
description:
The claude-commands skill documented 43 lines of Handlebars-style templating that Claude Code does not support, while this repo's own commands used the real $ARGUMENTS syntax. No check caught it, and an anti_fab waiver recorded it as accepted debt (see claude-skills-126, fixed in PR #134).

The idea: when a skill documents a file format the repo also contains, diff the documented tokens against the tokens actually used. One grep comparison would have caught claude-commands.

Why this is NOT trivial, and why it was split out of claude-skills-132: a naive double-brace grep produces mostly false positives. Measured across the repo, 13 of 14 files containing {{ use it legitimately — GitHub Actions dollar-brace expressions, Ansible Jinja2, Vue templates in slidev, mise templating. claude-commands was the only real case. A check that fires on all of them gets switched off as noise within a week, which is exactly how the original defect survived.

So the check needs per-format knowledge: for a given documented format, what is the real token vocabulary, and what does the repo actually use. Start with the formats this repo has ground truth for (Claude Code commands/skills, GitHub Actions workflows) rather than attempting generality.

Related constraint from claude-skills-127's false positives: path resolution must try skill-dir, plugin-root, AND repo-root before reporting anything missing. A checker that tries one manufactures false positives.

Deferred here from claude-skills-132 item 5.
close_reason:
Shipped as PR #147. Vocabulary-disjointness check across three formats, 0 new waivers (101 unchanged).

WHAT SHIPPED: for a format this repo both documents and contains, compare the documented token vocabulary against the real one; fire when the sets are disjoint OR the doc contains a foreign-family token. Formats: slash commands, agent frontmatter keys, hook event names. Key syntax/<format>:vocab_disjoint, wired into DETAIL_CHECKS.

VALIDATED AGAINST THE ACTUAL DEFECT: the pre-#134 claude-commands/SKILL.md is recoverable at 5ec8039~1, and at that commit the skill had no references/ dir. Reconstructing that true state gives documented {{}} vs real $ARGUMENTS — disjoint, fires, exit 1. Same rule at HEAD intersects on $ARGUMENTS and stays silent. One rule, opposite verdicts, no tuning.

SIGNALS MEASURED AND REJECTED: naive repo-wide {{ grep — 26 files, 26 false positives, zero current true positives (mise Go templates, GHA, Jinja2, Vue, dagu, awman all legitimate). Scoped {{ grep over 5 meta-skills — 1 hit, also false (a pseudocode-labelled example). A ratio rule instead of set-emptiness — unused-doc fractions today are 0.75/0.69/0.89 vs 1.0 for the defect, no usable margin.

THE HONEST LIMITS, recorded in test/README rather than oversold. This is a TRIPWIRE: real vocabularies are 1 command token, 1 hook event, 5 agent keys. Same-family fabrication is NOT caught — a doc inventing $ARGV/$INPUT while retaining one real token stays silent. Not closed mechanically because an uppercase-$ foreign rule would false-positive on doc bash examples, the same pollution the real side avoids.

THREE ROUNDS OF QUIET-FAILURE FIXES, which is the lesson. Plan revision 2 was written specifically to close 'the check goes silent' paths, and review still found two more afterward: (1) all three doc extractors read the documenting skill's OWN frontmatter, whose name/description/$ARGUMENTS/SessionStart mentions kept every intersection non-empty — the agents leg could never fire at all; (2) nothing guarded the globs, so \*\*→\* or a nonexistent directory left everything green. Fixed by stripping doc frontmatter and by measured file-count floors (a zero-files guard provably cannot catch the under-match, since the 9 files single-star matches include both $ARGUMENTS users). Then two more self-test gaps: an off-by-one strip and stale-low floors both escaped all 10 cases.

Generalisable: 'can this layer produce nothing?' must be asked at every layer feeding the comparison — the doc extractor, the file matcher, and the frontmatter above them — not once at whichever layer you happened to think of.

Follow-up filed: claude-skills-155 (validator crashes on a tracked-but-deleted file; predates this, came in with #144).

title: Review agents must never change git state — one moved the working tree out from under three writers
description:
INCIDENT, 2026-07-25. A review agent was dispatched with an explicit instruction: 'REVIEW ONLY — no edits, no commits, no git state changes.' It checked out the PR branch mid-review and then, in its words, 'immediately restored main'. The working tree had been on refactor/split-oversized-core-skills with three other agents actively writing to it. Restoring 'main' silently moved all three agents' work onto the wrong branch.

No work was lost — the branch pointed at main's tip, so switching back preserved every uncommitted change and no file contents moved. But the failure mode is exactly the working-tree contention this repo's conventions warn about, and it was caused by the one class of agent that should never touch git state.

Two things made it recoverable rather than destructive, and both were luck rather than design: the branch happened to be at the same commit as main, and the reviewer disclosed the checkout in its report. A reviewer that switched to a branch with different file contents would have corrupted three agents' in-flight work with no notification.

Fixes to make:
1. Review-agent prompt template: state that git checkout, switch, restore, stash, and reset are forbidden, not merely that the agent should not commit. 'No git state changes' was not specific enough — the agent read checkout-then-restore as net-zero.
2. Give reviewers a read-only way to inspect another branch: git show <ref>:<path>, git diff main...<branch>, git ls-tree. The review-132 agent did exactly this correctly and said so ('all file-existence checks were done against git objects, not the working tree') — that is the pattern to codify.
3. Consider whether parallel writers should use shallow clones per the repo convention rather than sharing one tree, given that any agent with Bash can move HEAD.

Codify in the agent-dispatch guidance that the lead uses when writing review prompts.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #140. dispatch-discipline.md gains a read-only-agents section: named mutating commands plus a category catch-all (a closed list recreates the literal-reading failure one step over), a clone-with-origin-removed recipe for destructive testing, and a .git write ban carving out git fetch. Rule carried verbatim into every read-only role in both workflow templates — forge reviewPrompt/testReviewPrompt/ciPrompt/handsPrompt and five-tier reviewPrompt/ciPrompt/plannerPrompt — since the shipped templates had said 'do NOT edit files or commit', which is exactly the wording a checkout defeats.

comments.text:
A better answer than the prohibition, discovered by the PR #137 reviewer: it needed to test destructively — create broken reference links, add orphan files, mutate the baseline, run --update-baseline — and did all of it in a SCRATCHPAD CLONE of the repo, leaving the live tree untouched. Verbatim from its report: 'All tests below were run live in a scratchpad copy of the repo; the real tree was never modified.'

That is strictly better than what this issue currently proposes. Forbidding git checkout/switch/restore/stash/reset stops a reviewer from moving the tree, but it also stops it from testing anything that requires mutation — so a reviewer either cannot verify a destructive scenario, or does it in the live tree and hopes nothing else is writing. The clone removes the tradeoff: full freedom to mutate, zero risk to in-flight work.

Codify BOTH in the review-agent prompt template:
1. Never run git checkout, switch, restore, stash, or reset against the shared working tree. Naming the commands matters — the agent that caused the incident read 'no git state changes' as permitting checkout-then-restore, since it restored afterwards.
2. To inspect another ref read-only: git show <ref>:<path>, git diff main...<branch>, git ls-tree.
3. To test anything requiring mutation: clone or copy the repo into the scratchpad and work there. State the scratchpad path in the report so the work is auditable.

Point 3 is the one that would have made the #137 review possible without any of the risk this issue was filed about.

title: Core-list check: delete G2 and anchor lists to a marker
description:
Two verified silent false passes remain in test/validate-core-list.nu. Both are now covered by characterisation fixtures in --self-test, so fixing either will fail the self-test and force the expectation to be updated deliberately.

F1 - the paren-annotation blessing. G2 accepts any bullet whose remainder starts with an open paren, regardless of what the annotation says. A bullet reading '- /core:tdd (NOT loaded by default; skip for doc-only work)' inside the run counts as a list entry, so a command file can instruct the model that tdd is not loaded while CI reports the list canonical. Per-run comparison narrowed the blast radius but did not remove the class. Root cause: the earlier fix that introduced the paren rule converted an over-broad match into a BLESSED IDIOM. Fix: delete G2 entirely (about 30 lines) and require load lists to be names-only lines, moving the two annotations in commands/work.md onto the following line.

F3 - the guarantee is weaker than the claim. What the check actually guarantees is 'at least one canonical run exists in this file and no visible run disagrees', NOT 'the operative list is canonical'. Annotate a real list with em-dashes (an idiom this repo already uses and which the grammar deliberately excludes) and it becomes invisible to both grammars; add a fenced for-reference block and the file passes. Verified: the operative list can be deleted ENTIRELY from plugins/tools/claude-code/templates/CLAUDE.md, leaving zero core bullets in the template an operator copies into their repo, and the check still exits 0. Fix: stop searching for a list. Anchor each satellite to a named marker (an HTML comment, or the line following '## Load skills') and validate THAT list.

Both fixes make the check SHORTER and sound, which is the right shape to carry into claude-skills-122. Do not add a third grammar.

Also open, lower severity:
- Coverage decay: applying the check's own grammars to all tracked .md and .sh files finds 24 files with qualifying runs that are in neither SATELLITES nor EXCLUDED_PARTIAL (qa and pm agents, agent-sandboxing commands, github pr-review, core bees-manager). All are currently partial subsets so nothing is stale today, but a new file listing the full stack is invisible forever. Consider inverting the design: sweep tracked files and require any run with 6 or more core names to match canonical unless waived, which deletes the SATELLITES allowlist role.
- Header comment states the union-false-pass rationale twice; the four-iteration design history is git's job. About 20 lines.
- test/README.md does not document test:core-list, though the repo CLAUDE.md points readers there.
- Fence info-string edge and the G1/G2 trailing-punctuation asymmetry, carried over from the original claude-skills-134 scope.

Fixed in PR #131 and NOT open here: the canonical block boundary now terminates at the closing fence rather than the next '## ' heading; extract-canonical-names now uniqs and fails on duplicates; the self-test is wired into mise.toml like its two siblings; SKILL.md no longer claims universal drift-checking; the prompt-template placeholder is self-refuting; the stray '#' maintainer note no longer leaks into turn-1 context.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #139 (a598efe). G2 deleted; per-satellite anchors with adjacency, fence-aware matching, and an anchor_in_fence opt-in; additive every-run rule retained; union-based coverage sweep; CommonMark-line-faithful fence model. Four adversarial rounds demonstrated and closed: anchor theft via a fenced lead-in, sweep bypass by a blank-line split, naive fence parity (four-backtick and tilde), and phantom openers (backtick info string and 4-space indent). 25 fixtures. Residuals stated in Known limits: container-relative fence indentation, single-name fenced mentions, semantics-blind anchor regexes.

title: CI hardening from the 2026-07-25 audit: structural checks, waiver hygiene, number single-sourcing
description:
Every defect found during the core-skill and claude-code plugin audit passed mise run ci green. The checks validate internal consistency, not correctness, and waivers hid three real bugs. Concrete changes, in priority order.

1. STRUCTURAL LOAD-LIST CHECK (replaces substring matching in test/validate-core-list.nu). The current check (:56-57) greps each canonical name as a substring anywhere in a satellite file, so a name mentioned in prose satisfies it identically to a name in an actual load list. During the 10-to-8 trim, five satellites went green while their load lists were stale. Fix: parse the fenced or bulleted skill list out of each satellite and compare SETS against the canonical block. This yields drift-by-addition detection as a side effect, which textual matching cannot provide.

2. DISCOVER SATELLITE COVERAGE, DO NOT ENUMERATE IT. SATELLITES (:22-31) is a hand-maintained array of eight paths. references/validator.md and references/fix-agent.md both carry core-skill load lists and were absent from it, so their content was invisible to CI (see claude-skills-125). Fix: treat any file containing a /core:-prefixed list as a satellite by discovery, so a new one cannot be missed.

3. WAIVER HYGIENE. test/quality-baseline.json has 141 entries and no metadata. claude-code/claude-commands:anti_fab made a fabricated-syntax bug (claude-skills-126) read as accepted debt; plugin-marketplace:links, claude-plugins:links, and skill-update:source hid five missing files (claude-skills-127). Fix: require a linked issue id and a first-seen date per waiver; report waivers with no linked issue; distinguish permanent-by-design entries from debt so the debt count means something.

4. NUMBER SINGLE-SOURCING CHECK. Three literals, two values, one enforcer: the SKILL.md body cap is 500 in test/validate-skills-quality.nu:417 (enforced), 500 in claude-skills SKILL.md, and 300 in plugins/tools/claude-code/hooks/session-start.sh:19 (enforced by nothing). The description cap appears as 1024 (validator) and 1536 (claude-skills:90). claude-skills-benchmark:23-35 documents 11 checks while the validator has 26 distinct failure keys. Fix: assert that numeric literals in prose match the validator constants, or that prose cites the constant instead of restating it.

5. SYNTAX-VS-USAGE CROSS-VALIDATION. A skill documenting a syntax, in a repo that uses that syntax, should agree with it. claude-commands documents 43 Handlebars-style {{}} constructs and zero $ARGUMENTS, while plugins/core/commands/work.md and restraint-audit.md both use $ARGUMENTS. One grep comparison would have caught it. Generalize where cheap: when a skill teaches a file format the repo also contains, diff the documented tokens against the tokens actually used.

Overlaps to respect: claude-skills-124 already covers derivable-content and cross-file duplicate-block checks; claude-skills-130 covers scoping the reserved and ref_depth checks and the benchmark table drift. This issue covers items 1-5 above only.
close_reason: Waiver hygiene shipped in PR #137 (2aae793): record schema with required class/issue, both-direction count ratchet across 26 entries, honest two-figure burn-down, 20 self-test fixtures. Other four items dispositioned to 135, 123, 141 and (done) #131. Residuals documented in the baseline _comment.

comments.text:
Waiver re-adjudication (all 141 entries) surfaced the ROOT MECHANISM behind claude-skills-127, which sharpens item 3 of this issue.

THE GRANULARITY GAP: baseline keys are plugin/skill:check, not per-finding. A single waived links key absorbs unlimited NEW broken links in that skill. That is precisely how 35 missing reference files sat under 9 waiver keys — each key was earned once, then silently covered every subsequent regression. The validator already computes the per-finding details column at runtime; it simply is not ratcheted.

Concrete fix, replacing the vaguer 'waiver metadata' wording in item 3: convert allowed_failures entries from bare strings to objects with {key, class: BUG|DEBT|CHECK_DEFECT, issue: claude-skills-N, added: YYYY-MM-DD, detail_count: N}. CI then asserts:
(a) class and issue are required — filing an issue at waiver time is what would have surfaced 126, 127, and skill-update:source on the day they were baselined, and forcing an explicit BUG/DEBT call makes hiding a bug a false statement rather than an omission;
(b) detail_count ratchet — fail if the current finding count for a waived key exceeds the stored count, closing the gap above;
(c) CHECK_DEFECT entries reference an issue against the CHECK and are excluded from the burn-down total.

Why (c) matters: roughly 30 of the 141 entries are permanent false positives that can never burn down — 11 reserved (name contains 'claude'), 16 examples (hub skills whose fenced examples live in references/, which the check does not scan), 2 invocations (external /allium: commands), 2 ref_depth, 1 links. The headline 141 overstates real debt by about a fifth, which makes the number useless as a signal.

Ratchet mechanism itself verified WORKING: validate-skills-quality.nu:719 computes stale keys, :731-737 fails the run listing them, --update-baseline (:700-707) refuses net-new keys. Zero entries are currently stale. The defect is granularity, not the ratchet.

Waiver hygiene shipped in PR #137 (merged, 2aae793). What landed:

- Schema: 125 waivers migrated from bare strings to records carrying {key, class, issue, first_seen, detail_count}. class validated against BUG|DEBT|CHECK_DEFECT; class and issue required; bare strings, duplicate keys, invalid class values, and detail_count mismatches (null on a countable check, non-null on a boolean one) are all load-time hard failures. No dual-shape support, so a hand-added entry cannot bypass the requirements.
- Count ratchet in BOTH directions across 26 of 125 entries (14 lines, 8 ref_depth, 2 orphans, 2 invocations): current > stored fails as regression, current < stored fails as stale until lowered, --update-baseline lowers shrink-only and never raises. Class-blind, so a defective check cannot absorb new findings either.
- Burn-down prints both figures: 94 debt/bug + 31 check-defects excluded. The 31 can never be fixed by editing a skill, so counting them as debt overstated real backlog by a quarter.
- 20 self-test fixtures (5 frontmatter + 15 baseline), both suites always run.

An adversarial review DEFEATED the first version: ref_depth computes a detail list but had been left out of DETAIL_CHECKS while carrying 8 live waivers, so a new nested-reference violation was absorbed with CI green — the same 34-behind-9 shape this issue was filed about, reproduced inside the mechanism built to stop it. Fixed and independently re-verified (core/git:ref_depth: current 3 > baselined 2).

Residuals, stated in the baseline _comment rather than implied away:
1. A count-neutral swap passes — the ratchet bounds the NUMBER of findings per waived check, not their identity. Closing it needs per-finding hashes, a different design.
2. Pass-2 surfaces (bad_invocations, skills-frontmatter) are countable but unratcheted; no Pass-2 waiver exists so hard-failure guards them, and a code comment marks the treatment a future one needs.
3. The fabricated-content class is NOT closed. claude-skills-126 sat behind an anti_fab waiver and no check inspects content veracity. The required-issue field is the only mitigation this PR ships for it; detection is claude-skills-141.
4. CI cannot assert an issue pointer is still OPEN (no tracker access), so the requirement catches a missing pointer, not a rotting one. The first pass pointed 66 entries at closed issues 121 and 131 — caught by audit, repointed to 143 and 144. Periodic re-audit is the only guard.

Remaining items of this issue are dispositioned to claude-skills-135 (coverage discovery), 123 (number single-sourcing), and 141 (syntax-vs-usage). This issue can close once those pointers are considered adequate.

REOPENING CONSIDERATION on the pointer-rot residual recorded when this closed. It has now happened twice in two days, which makes it a live defect rather than a noted limitation.

Instance 1 (caught by audit during PR #137): 66 entries pointed at claude-skills-121 and 131, both CLOSED, and neither owned the remaining work. Repointed to 143 and 144.
Instance 2 (caught by the claude-skills-130 plan review): the 6 genuine ref_depth DEBT entries pointed at claude-skills-134 — 'Harden core-list check' — which mentions ref_depth zero times. Never a correct pointer, not a decayed one. Repointed to 145.

So the class/issue requirement catches a MISSING pointer but neither a CLOSED one nor a WRONG one. Both instances were found by a human-directed audit, which does not scale and is exactly the pattern this repo keeps rediscovering: a mechanism satisfying its own letter while missing its purpose.

Two options, neither implemented:
1. CI-side: the validator cannot query bees (CI has no tracker access), so it cannot assert a pointer is open. It COULD assert the pointer is well-formed and that the referenced id appears in the tracked .bees/issues.jsonl, which IS in the repo — that catches typos and deleted issues, though not closed ones.
2. Tracker-side: a bees-based audit run as part of the burn-down review — for each distinct issue in quality-baseline.json, assert OPEN and assert the issue text actually names the check it is cited for. That catches both failure modes but runs outside CI.

Option 1 is cheap and closes the typo/nonexistent case in CI. Option 2 is the one that would have caught both real instances. Recommend both, tracked here or in a new issue if this stays closed.

title: Fix quality checks that misfire on skill-authoring and Claude-domain skills
description:
Three checks in test/validate-skills-quality.nu produce waivers with no burn-down path. A waiver class that can never be fixed is noise, not a ratchet.

1. reserved check (:413-415) fails any skill whose NAME contains 'claude' or 'anthropic'. All ten claude-code plugin skills are permanently baselined for it (quality-baseline.json:13-28). The upstream intent is stopping third-party skills from implying official status; a plugin whose entire domain IS Claude Code must say 'claude'. Fix: exempt the claude-code plugin in the check, delete the ten baseline entries.

2. ref_depth waivers on claude-skills and skill-update are FALSE POSITIVES, verified by reading the offending files. claude-skills/references/examples.md:102 and :106 mention references/contexts.md and references/liveview-guide.md inside quoted content of an example Phoenix skill being annotated; :134 is meta-guidance about moving material to references/. skill-update/references/update-checklist.md:38 is a heading describing a file in the TARGET skill being updated, not a reference of skill-update. Root cause: has-unqualified-references-token (:118-131) flags any prose mention of 'references/' inside a reference file — unavoidable for skills whose domain is skill authoring. Fix: skip tokens inside fenced/quoted context, or mark these two permanent-by-design in the baseline comment so the intent is explicit.

3. claude-teams:ref_depth is a REAL one-line defect, unlike the two above: references/subagents.md:144 links to sibling references/agent-sdk.md, an actual reference-to-reference hop. Reword, then remove the waiver.

4. claude-skills-benchmark's Static Analysis Checks table (:23-35) documents 11 checks and its scorecard example (:89-90) reports '9/11' and '10/11'. The validator has 26 distinct failure keys (allowed_tools, anti_fab, bad_event, bad_invocations, bad_model, bad_wrapper, desc, examples, invocations, kebab, lines, links, missing_desc, missing_name, name_dir, name_len, orphans, ref_depth, reserved, skills_duplicate, skills_shape, skills_unresolved, source, third_person, use_when, version_pin), a subset of which apply to skills. The table is the drift generator: replace it with the checks' intent plus 'defined in test/validate-skills-quality.nu; run mise test:skills-quality', so the list lives where it is enforced.
close_reason: All four misfiring checks fixed in PR #138 (738259f); 31 CHECK_DEFECT waivers retired, 125 to 94, burn-down now reports one honest number. reserved narrowed to exact match on claude/anthropic (no anthropic-* prefix rule — it would fire on legitimate anthropic-api/anthropic-sdk). examples accepts a fenced reference only when SKILL.md carries the references/<basename> token. ref_depth got fence-length-aware stripping, heading-line exemption, and a no-concrete-target exemption, plus one content edit repairing a genuinely malformed examples.md. invocations enumerates upstream allium targets into invocables rather than exempting the namespace. Teeth verified: an adversarial review ran ~10 attack shapes per check in a scratchpad clone and could not construct a genuine violation that escapes.

title: Progressive-disclosure trim: claude-skills, plugin-marketplace, claude-plugins
description:
Three skills are central repositories rather than routers — the shape Anthropic's Claude-5 context-engineering guidance argues against (a skill should load context at the right time, not hold it all upfront). Measured: claude-skills 465 lines / 5 references, plugin-marketplace 481 / 1, claude-plugins 412 / 1. Compare the in-repo exemplars: claude-teams 96 lines / 4 refs, claude-workflows 114 / 3.

claude-skills is the priority — it loads whenever anyone authors a skill, so its bloat costs most:
- Cut the 37-line inline anti-fabrication block (SKILL.md:397-433), a verbatim copy of core:anti-fabrication. Validator check 10 passes on a single reference, which line 401 already provides. ~34 lines, zero enforcement loss.
- Deduplicate the 'description is the ONLY text at Level 1' callout (stated at :101 and again at :337-339).
- Compress the seven-step workflow (:176-260, ~85 lines) to imperative bullets; its worked git-skill examples constrain rather than inform.
- Stop summarizing each reference in the body (:272-282, :284-293, :318-328 each carry a bullet digest AND a see-references pointer). One-line pointers.
Target ~250 lines without touching enforcement content.

plugin-marketplace and claude-plugins share one pattern: their Common Validation Errors catalogs, Creating a New X walkthroughs, and Troubleshooting sections re-teach what scripts/validate-marketplace.nu and scripts/validate-plugin.nu already report precisely. The script output is the teacher. Move the error catalogs into each skill's references/, keep the schema essentials, the strict-mode decision guidance (plugin-marketplace:252-262 — genuine judgment worth keeping), and the script table.

Keep prescriptive: claude-plugins' Invalid Fields list (:112-119) is schema-mandated and validator-enforced.

title: Split claude-agents and sharpen its activation description
description:
claude-agents is 441 lines with zero references/ — the largest skill in the claude-code plugin and the only large one with no progressive disclosure. Content is accurate against upstream; the problem is bloat from restatement plus a weak trigger.

Delete (restates the frontmatter field table at :108-127, which is the single source):
- Tool Allowlist section :143-169 (:159-162 are blank lines; the no-restrictions example at :163-169 is an empty frontmatter block)
- Model Selection, duplicated at :171-184 AND :321-328 — keep one line
- Turn Limits :330-339 (restates the maxTurns row as commented YAML)
- Example frontmatter :129-141 (restates the table in comment form)

Move to references/patterns.md: Agent Writing Style (:85-102), Common Agent Patterns (:203-227), Best Practices examples (:286-360).
Move to references/plugin-config.md: plugin.json wiring (:229-251), Invoking Agents (:253-270), Agent Communication (:272-284), Troubleshooting (:409-428).
Security (:362-397): keep a three-line least-privilege statement in body, move worked examples.

Keep prescriptive in body — facts an agent would otherwise fabricate: the frontmatter field table and its enums (:108-127), and the skills-vs-tools preloading semantics including 'never list Skill in tools:' (:114, :186-201).

Fix one fabricated metric: the Clear Instructions example at :345-360 hardcodes 'minimum 80% code coverage' — an invented number inside a teaching example, which this repo's anti-fabrication rules prohibit.

It would miss on 'subagent', on frontmatter-field questions (permissionMode, maxTurns, skills), and on skill preloading. Proposed: 'Guide for creating custom agents (subagents) for Claude Code. Use when writing agents/*.md files, choosing agent frontmatter (tools, model, skills, permissionMode, maxTurns), restricting a subagent tool allowlist, preloading skills into an agent, or troubleshooting agent invocation.'

Target body ~170-200 lines.

title: Validator and fix-agent tiers load only subsets of the mandatory core stack
description:
agent-loop SKILL.md states "Every agent at every tier loads these before any work" for the ten mandatory core skills, but two tier references contradict it and have since before this work:

- references/validator.md:7 loads only /core:tdd, /core:mise, /core:anti-fabrication (3 of 10).
- references/fix-agent.md:9 loads only /core:anti-fabrication, /core:git, /core:tdd, /core:mise (4 of 10).

Neither file is in the SATELLITES list in test/validate-core-list.nu, so the drift check cannot see them — the discrepancy has been invisible to CI.

Decide and codify one of two positions: either these tiers genuinely need the full ten (then fix both lists and add both files to SATELLITES), or per-tier subsets are legitimate (then soften the every-agent-at-every-tier claim in SKILL.md and document which tiers may subset, so the exemption is explicit rather than accidental).

Found during claude-skills-120 review.
close_reason:
Shipped as PR #145. Operator ruling: per-tier subsets are legitimate, discriminator is whether the tier writes code — the CI runner does not need /core:tdd, the agent addressing its findings does.

Codified as a PER-SKILL exemption, not per-tier: a tier may omit an individual skill its role cannot exercise, nothing more. validator.md omits /core:tdd (runs the suite, writes no code); fix-agent.md keeps /core:tdd and gained /core:restraint (writes code, and already restated restraint's ladder as prose at four places). Each states what it omits and why in its own pre-flight step, so the omission is on the record rather than accidental.

The first draft was per-tier and contradicted itself — the headline bound code-writing agents to all ten while the exemption freed no-code tiers, then named fix-agent (which writes code) as an exemption user. Gate 3 caught it; the per-skill rewrite dissolves it and restores the general mandate for every tier.

No new check was needed. The risk from subsetting is a tier naming a skill that does not exist or has gone stale, and the invocations check in validate-skills-quality.nu already scans references/ and fails on any unresolvable token — verified both by inserting a bogus name and by simulating removal of ./skills/tdd from the core manifest, which fails every /core:tdd mention repo-wide. So neither file needed adding to SATELLITES.

What remains unchecked, stated plainly in SKILL.md rather than papered over: subset MEMBERSHIP. A tier dropping a skill it should carry passes CI. Tracked as claude-skills-152 with the proposed {path, expected: [...]} satellite shape.

title: Split oversized core skills into references/ (mise, nushell, twelve-factor)
description:
Eight core skills carry :lines waivers in test/quality-baseline.json, exceeding the 500-line CI cap in test/validate-skills-quality.nu:417 and grandfathered by the shrink-only ratchet: mise (954), nushell (929), twelve-factor (867), container (793), beads (735), documentation (676), code-review (611), bees (581).

All ten mandatory core skills load in every session and every spawned agent, so mise, nushell, twelve-factor, and bees bodies are injected everywhere. Splitting detail into references/ cuts that cost without changing which skills are mandatory — this is the correct fix for the token cost, established when the alternative (demoting skills out of the mandatory set) was reviewed and rejected.

Per skill: keep the body under the cap, move detail one level deep into references/ (never reference-to-reference), then remove that skill's :lines entry from test/quality-baseline.json — the ratchet fails the run if a stale waiver survives a fix.

Priority order: mise, nushell, twelve-factor, and bees first (always-loaded), then code-review, documentation, container, beads.
close_reason: mise 954->236, nushell 929->193, twelve-factor 867->262; each now has 5 references. ~2060 lines removed from every session's always-load cost with no change to which skills are mandatory. Three :lines waivers removed; ratchet 128->125. bees/beads/code-review/container/documentation remain over cap but are not always-loaded — file separately if wanted.

title: Collapse duplicate mandatory-skill-list copies to one canonical source plus pointers
description:
The mandatory core-skill list is enumerated in 8+ places kept in sync by test/validate-core-list.nu. Anthropic's context-engineering guidance for Claude 5 generation models argues for single statements over repetition — put an instruction in one place rather than restating it across layers. The implied fix is fewer copies, not a better synchronizer.

Target shape: the canonical fenced block in agent-loop SKILL.md stays; every other site carries only the existing pointer line (Canonical list: /core:agent-loop Core Skills Mandatory). Then validate-core-list.nu shrinks to asserting the canonical count plus the presence of the pointer string.

Unresolved design tension to settle in this issue: globs do not expand in Agent prompts, so a spawn prompt saying load the mandatory skills per /core:agent-loop costs the worker a lookup hop it can skip. Pointers are clearly correct for docs and reference files. Whether the spawn-prompt template keeps its explicit enumeration (reliability) or moves to a pointer (single source) is the actual decision.

Depends on claude-skills-120 landing first (that PR hand-edits the same satellites for the 10-to-8 trim).
close_reason: Shipped in PR #141. title: Add derivable-content and duplicate-block checks to skill quality validation
description:
Two static checks to add to test/validate-skills-quality.nu, mirroring heuristics the Claude Code /doctor checkup applies to CLAUDE.md files (changelog: a /doctor check proposes trimming checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content Claude could derive from the codebase).

1. Derivable content: flag skill body content that restates what an agent can read directly from the repo — directory listings, file inventories, obvious structure — rather than genuine gotchas. Heuristic, so it reports rather than hard-fails at first.
2. Cross-file duplicate blocks: detect near-identical blocks repeated across SKILL.md, template CLAUDE.md, and hook scripts. This is the static check that would have caught the 8-copy mandatory-list pattern on its own.

Both feed the existing shrink-only ratchet in test/quality-baseline.json so pre-existing hits are recorded without blocking, and new ones cannot land. Keep findings anti-fabrication compliant: report measured counts and file:line evidence, never a quality score with no derivation.

CHECK 2 (cross-file duplicate blocks) SHIPPED: 8-normalised-line windows over git-tracked .md/.sh under plugins/ plus root CLAUDE.md, grouped per file-set so one duplicated section is one finding. comments.text: Third doctrine update from the same production epic: the P2 test-author prompt's 'compile errors for not-yet-existing modules count as the deliberate red' clause is a loophole — authors wave off their OWN nonexistent-API errors as the red. Tighten: deliberate red = assertion failures or missing symbols in the PROJECT's own modules; any compile error naming stdlib/third-party APIs is the author's bug and blocks handoff. Also add: fix agents that cannot fix within prohibitions must ESCALATE, never shim (observed: fake-std compat module to dodge frozen-test flaws — same disease as patching the installed stdlib).

Fourth data point, same production epic (2026-06-13), reinforcing the no-shim doctrine with a new variant + a verification technique:

VARIANT OF THE DISEASE: beyond a fake-std compat MODULE, a fix agent vendored ~6000 lines of the toolchain's actual stdlib into the repo (a src tree + a build-system lib-dir overlay redirecting the compiler at a forked stdlib) to fake two removed/renamed stdlib APIs. Same root cause as patching the installed stdlib or writing a compat shim: dodging a removed API instead of migrating the call site. Doctrine: NEVER vendor, fork, overlay, or redirect the language stdlib/toolchain. A removed API means migrate to the replacement (here: a removed Mutex primitive → a tiny test-local lock built on the still-present atomic primitives, methods on the test's OWN fake type, zero additions to std) or ESCALATE. The correct fix was ~30 lines; the shim was ~6000.

MASKED-ERROR GOTCHA + verification technique: in a deliberate-red test file that imports not-yet-existing project modules, the missing-module import error SHORT-CIRCUITS compilation before the test body is semantically analyzed. This MASKS latent stdlib-API breakages elsewhere in the same file (a second dead-API usage stayed invisible behind the import failure). The author's own grep/visual review can miss it, and it will only surface for the downstream implementer who is forbidden from editing the test file. Technique that catches it: write THROWAWAY stub modules satisfying just the referenced symbols, compile the test file against them (it should build + run, failing only on assertions/logic), then DELETE the stubs to restore the legitimate red. This proves the test body is API-correct independent of the missing project modules. Pairs with the existing 'compile errors naming stdlib/third-party APIs are the author's bug' tightening above.
