title: core:container: 1.0.0 run flags wrong -- --stop-signal not a run option (signal lives on container stop); --shm-size verified present
description:
## Problem

The skill documents two flags as 1.0.0+ additions to `container run`:

1. `--stop-signal` — claimed as a `container run` option in multiple places
2. `--shm-size` — claimed as a `container run` option

Verified against container CLI 1.0.0 (commit ee848e3):
- `--stop-signal` does NOT exist on `container run` — `container run --help` has no such flag
- `--shm-size` IS present on `container run` (confirmed via `container run --help | grep shm`: shows `--shm-size <shm-size>  Size of /dev/shm (e.g. 64M, 1G)`)
- Signal control lives on `container stop` via `-s / --signal <signal>` (confirmed via `container stop --help`)

File:line locations of wrong claims:

- `plugins/core/skills/container/SKILL.md:187` — example uses `--stop-signal SIGTERM` on `container run`
- `plugins/core/skills/container/references/command-reference.md:53` — table row: `--stop-signal | | Signal sent to stop the container (1.0.0+)`
- `plugins/core/skills/container/references/version-history.md:29` — release note claims `--stop-signal on container run`
- `plugins/core/skills/container/templates/1.0.0/commands.md:21` — bullet: `--stop-signal option on container run`
- `plugins/core/skills/container/templates/1.0.0/commands.md:94` — table: `container run | --stop-signal and --shm-size options added`
- `plugins/core/skills/container/templates/1.0.0/commands.md:99` — example: `container run --stop-signal SIGTERM -d --name app myapp:latest`

## Evidence

CLI version:
  container CLI version 1.0.0 (build: release, commit: ee848e3)

`container run --help | grep -iE 'stop-signal|shm'`:
  --shm-size <shm-size>   Size of /dev/shm (e.g. 64M, 1G)
  (no --stop-signal line)

`container stop --help` (signal IS here):
  -s, --signal <signal>   Signal to send to the containers

## Fix

- `--stop-signal`: Remove from all `container run` examples and flag tables. The correct form for custom stop signals is `container stop --signal <SIG>` (or `-s <SIG>`). The SKILL.md example at line 187 and the templates/1.0.0/commands.md example at line 99 should be removed or replaced with a `container stop` example. The command-reference.md table row should move to the `container stop` flags section. The version-history.md entry should be corrected to say the signal flag is on `container stop`, not `container run`.
- `--shm-size`: No change needed — verified present on `container run` in 1.0.0.

## Affected files

- `plugins/core/skills/container/SKILL.md` line 187 (and ~190 for shm-size example — shm-size example is correct, stop-signal example is wrong)
- `plugins/core/skills/container/references/command-reference.md` line 53

title: [task][P3] /core:nushell — document bash test/&&/|| silent error-mask gotcha
description:
## What

Add a "Common Pitfalls" subsection to the /core:nushell skill (and possibly /core:git-operations or a generic shell skill) documenting that bash `&& ... ||` patterns silently mask command failures.

## Reproduction

Pattern that bit us:
```bash
test -f /path/to/binary && codesign --force --sign - /path/to/binary || echo skip
```

Intent: codesign the binary if it exists; otherwise skip.

Reality: if codesign FAILS (binary already signed with immutable signature, permission denied, etc.), the `|| echo skip` fires and the WHOLE command exits 0. The script proceeds as if codesign succeeded, and downstream steps (start-service) run with an unsigned binary → macOS Tahoe SIGKILL → service won't start.

The Nushell guard `if $cs_burrito.exit_code != 0` never fires because the bash exit code is 0.

## Correct shape

Use bash `if/else`, not `&& ... ||`:
```bash
if test -f /path/to/binary; then
  codesign --force --sign - /path/to/binary
else
  echo "skip — binary absent"
fi
```

This propagates codesign's exit code correctly. Failures surface to the calling script.

## Why it matters

The `cmd1 && cmd2 || cmd3` shorthand is a CLASSIC bash footgun. It looks like "if cmd1 then cmd2 else cmd3" but it's actually "if (cmd1 && cmd2) succeeds then 0; else cmd3". When `cmd2` legitimately fails, `cmd3` runs and the OVERALL exit is 0 (assuming cmd3 succeeds). The "else" branch fires on ANY non-zero exit upstream, not just the missing-precondition case.

For non-zero-tolerant commands (codesign, ssh, scp, kubectl apply, mix release, etc.) this masks real failures.

## Suggested insertion

`/core:nushell` skill, "Common Pitfalls" section. Title: "Bash `&& ... ||` Silent Error Mask in Embedded Shell Commands". Body:

> When invoking bash from Nushell (e.g., `^bash -c "..."` or via mise's task runner), avoid `cmd1 && cmd2 || cmd3` for conditional execution. Use bash `if/else` instead so the inner command's exit code propagates correctly.
>
> WRONG (silent error mask):
> ```bash
> test -f path && do-thing || echo skip
> ```
> If `do-thing` fails, `echo skip` fires and the OVERALL command exits 0. Caller cannot detect the failure.
>
> CORRECT (propagates exit code):
> ```bash
> if test -f path; then do-thing; else echo skip; fi
> ```
>
> This bit us in deploy-to-mini's codesign step (PR #80 / runex-workflows): codesign failed silently, binary stayed unsigned, macOS 26 Tahoe SIGKILLed it on start.

## Reference

- runex-workflows PR #80 (the fix)
- feedback_macos26_codesign_on_deploy.md (related macOS gotcha; this is the deeper why-it-wasn't-caught)
- Bash POSIX spec on logical-operator precedence: `&&` and `||` left-associative, both at same precedence; `cmd1 && cmd2 || cmd3` parses as `(cmd1 && cmd2) || cmd3`

## Acceptance

- /core:nushell SKILL.md "Common Pitfalls" section gains the bash `&& ... ||` subsection with WRONG/CORRECT examples + reference to PR #80
- (Optional) cross-link from /core:git-operations or a generic shell-scripts skill if/when one exists
- Bumped /core:* plugin version per claude-skills versioning rules

- Lead agent collects bees writes from worker reports (BEES REQUESTS: blocks)
- Lead spawns `bees-manager` (defined as a local Claude Code agent in operator's plugin/agents directory)
- bees-manager serializes the writes through the bees CLI (single-writer SQLite respected)

title: [task][P2] Create /elixir:ecto skill — Ecto schemas + changesets default, raw SQL is fallback
description:
CRITICAL: Implementer agents have twice written raw SQL where Ecto schemas + changesets are the right pattern. The first incident was direct epic writes (addressed by operator memory `feedback_dogfood_ecto_through_tidewave.md`); the second was an Ecto migration writing `repo().query!("UPDATE ...")`. Operator memories don't propagate to fresh sessions or other agents — a marketplace skill does. This skill becomes the canonical reference loaded by every Elixir worker.

## Objective
Create a new top-level skill `/elixir:ecto` in `vinnie357/claude-skills` plugin marketplace covering Ecto patterns: schemas, changesets, migrations, Repo API, query DSL, raw-SQL escape-hatch criteria. Discoverability: an agent doing data work loads `/elixir:ecto` directly without needing operator memory.

## Context / Root Cause
Existing Elixir skills in the marketplace cover:
- elixir:style (bang functions, pattern matching, idiomatic returns)
- elixir:elixir-testing (ExUnit, mocks)
- elixir:elixir-config (runtime vs compile-time)
- elixir:elixir-anti-patterns
- elixir:phoenix-framework
- elixir:tidewave

NONE of these emphasize the Ecto-vs-raw-SQL rule strongly enough for an implementer to internalize on first load. PR #268 (vantageex github-337 implementation) initially shipped a migration with `repo().query!("SELECT ...", [])` — operator caught + corrected. The skill prevents the next regression.

## Acceptance Criteria
The skill (`vinnie357/claude-skills/plugins/elixir/skills/ecto/SKILL.md`) covers MINIMUM:

1. **Default rule**: "Ecto schemas + changesets are the DEFAULT; raw SQL via Ecto.Adapters.SQL.query is the FALLBACK"
2. **Reads**: idiomatic Ecto query DSL (from, where, join, fragment), Repo.all/get/one
3. **Writes**: changeset construction, Repo.insert/update/delete, return tuple semantics ({:ok, _} | {:error, %Changeset{}})
4. **Batch writes**: Repo.update_all with set: keyword, when to prefer over per-row update
5. **Migrations**:
   - Schema changes via `add`, `alter`, `drop` macros
   - Data transformations via Ecto query DSL with LOCAL SNAPSHOT SCHEMA pattern (avoid importing the live application schema — locks migration to its-time state, future schema changes don't break replay)
   - When `execute/1` is appropriate (DB-specific DDL, raw indexes, extensions)
6. **Multi-step**: Ecto.Multi for atomic combos (insert + update + side effect with rollback semantics)
7. **When raw SQL IS appropriate** (escape-hatch criteria):
   - Perf-critical hot paths where Ecto-generated SQL is too slow (rare)
   - Complex CTEs / window functions Ecto doesn't expose
   - DB-specific features (PostGIS, extensions)
   - One-off ops in tidewave eval (single-cell read; never write)
8. **Anti-patterns to avoid**:
   - `repo().query!("SELECT ...", [])` in migrations (use Repo.all + local snapshot schema)
   - Bypassing changeset validation by direct insert_all/update_all when validation matters
   - Importing live application schema into old migrations (replay breakage)
   - Using raw SQL "because it's faster" without measurement
9. **Use when triggers** (in frontmatter description per claude-code:claude-skills convention):
   - "Use when writing Ecto migrations, querying or mutating Ecto schemas, designing changesets, or choosing between Ecto query DSL and raw SQL"
10. **Examples**: include 3-5 concrete code blocks per pattern (good vs bad pairs)

Format requirements (per /claude-code:claude-skills skill spec):
- Frontmatter with name, description (third person + "Use when..."), license
- NO `allowed-tools` field (per /claude-code:claude-skills validate-plugin.nu rule)
- Body under 300 lines (overflow to references/)
- Zero hedging verbs (no "should", "may", "might", "consider", "try to" — use imperative)
- References one level deep only

## Deliverables
- New skill at `~/github/claude-skills/plugins/elixir/skills/ecto/SKILL.md` (verify path matches existing elixir skills layout)
- references/ subdirectory if needed for examples that overflow 300 lines

Second, the comparison is order sensitive: two keyword lists with identical members in a different order fail with a message that says mismatch even though the sets are equal. Harmless today since all 30 pairs match in order, and defensible on the grounds that the entry is meant to be an exact copy, but the failure message would be confusing when it fires. Either compare as sets or say order matters in the message. Verified by constructing each case against the real validator and observing the exit code.

title: core plugin description names 4 of its 13 skills
description: The core plugin description reads Essential development skills: Git, documentation, code review, security. title: bees accepts invalid enum values silently across several commands
description:
Found during the claude-skills-157/158 audit and independently reproduced. bees 0.4.0 performs no enum validation on several documented value sets, so a typo is stored verbatim and fails silently later rather than at the point of error.

Measured in a throwaway repo:
- 'bees update <id> --status bogus' -> 'Updated <id>', exit 0; 'list --json' then shows status 'bogus'. The issue is silently excluded from 'bees ready' from that point on, with no indication why.
- 'bees dep add <id> <blocker> -t nonsense' -> exit 0, type stored verbatim.
- 'bees create x -t garbage' -> accepted and stored.

Also a naming inconsistency worth resolving while here: 'dep --help' spells the third dependency type 'parent-child' while our docs say 'parent' — BOTH are accepted, because nothing validates. And 'create --help' lists type 'story' while the 'bees prime' cheatsheet says 'chore'; both accepted.

This is upstream behaviour, not a docs defect, so it is deliberately NOT part of the #157/#158 truth-up. Two possible dispositions: (a) document the trap in the bees skill — a typo'd status silently removes an issue from the ready queue, which is exactly the 'not discoverable from --help' content the skill body is for; or (b) raise it upstream against bees. (a) is cheap and within our control; (b) is the real fix. They are not exclusive.

Valid values observed from --help: status open, in_progress, closed, deferred; dep types blocks, related, parent/parent-child; issue types task, bug, feature, epic, story.

title: sources.md Version lines are stale repo-wide against plugin.json
description:
Found by Gate 3 on PR #149. Each plugin's skills/sources.md carries a 'Version: X' line that is not maintained when the plugin version bumps, so they drift silently. Measured at PR #149's head: slidev sources.md says 0.2.0 while plugin.json says 0.2.1; zig says 0.1.0 vs 0.1.4; core says 0.1.19 vs 0.2.32. Not created by #149 — the repo has never maintained them per bump, and #149 only made one of them one patch staler.

Decide one of three, then it is mechanical: (a) drop the Version line from sources.md entirely, since plugin.json is the source of truth and a second copy is exactly the duplication this repo keeps removing; (b) keep it and add a check that it matches plugin.json, which turns silent drift into a CI failure; (c) keep it and document that it means something else (e.g. the upstream tool version being tracked, not the plugin version) — check what it was originally for before assuming it mirrors plugin.json.

Note there is already a version_pin check that validates 'Current stable: X' claims against sources.md entries, so (b) would extend an existing mechanism rather than add a new one. Prefer (a) if the line has no consumer — restraint says delete the second copy rather than build a check to keep two copies equal.

title: validate-skills-quality crashes when a git-tracked file is deleted from the working tree
description:
Found while running the historical replay for claude-skills-141. The duplicate_block corpus scan (validate-skills-quality.nu ~line 1731) builds its file list from 'git ls-files' and then does 'open --raw' on each path. If a tracked file has been deleted from the working tree but the deletion is not yet committed, the validator dies with a raw nushell 'File not found' stack trace pointing at the open call, exit 1.

Reproduced on MAIN, so it predates 141 and came in with the duplicate_block check in PR #144: clone the repo, 'rm plugins/tools/claude-code/skills/claude-commands/references/examples.md', run 'nu test/validate-skills-quality.nu' -> 2 'File not found' lines, exit 1.

Why it matters: deleting a file and running CI before committing the deletion is an ordinary mid-refactor state, and any removal PR hits it — claude-skills-136 deleted tracked files and would have hit this had the removals not been staged first. The failure is also misleading: it looks like validator corruption rather than 'you have an uncommitted deletion'.

Fix: filter the corpus to paths that exist on disk, or use 'git ls-files' intersected with a filesystem check, and report skipped-because-deleted paths explicitly rather than crashing. Do not silently ignore missing files without saying so — a silent skip in a corpus scan is how a check goes quiet.

Same class as the other duplicate_block hardening in claude-skills-151; could be fixed together.
close_reason:
Shipped as PR #148. The duplicate-block corpus scan built its list from 'git ls-files' then opened every path, so a tracked-but-deleted file — an uncommitted deletion, the ordinary mid-refactor state — aborted the validator with a raw nushell trace. Reproduced on main first; came in with #144 (git log -S on the corpus line -> commit 2739702).

Fixed in BOTH scripts. Gate 3 found the sibling I had missed: sweep-unregistered in validate-core-list.nu had the identical git-ls-files-then-open shape, so a removal PR's local CI still died one script later in the same mise test run. Closing only the reported instance while its sibling survived is the exact 'fixed one instance of a class' pattern this repo keeps hitting. Both now partition missing paths out and ANNOUNCE the skip with each path — a corpus that shrinks silently would be worse than one that crashes.

After the fix the original repro exits 1 for the right reason: the links check reports that the skill references a file no longer on disk.

Residual recorded, not hidden: deleting main's one-line print caller still passes every self-test. The warning CONTENT is now pinned in split-corpus-paths (the 'helper returns no warnings' mutation fails), but main's wiring is not unit-testable. That is the third instance of one root cause — see claude-skills-151, which now carries all three and the integration-harness fix shape that would close them together.

comments.text: OPERATOR DECISION (2026-07-27): help users bootstrap BEES. Scope for whoever takes this: /core:setup and plugins/core/agents/setup.md should bootstrap bees as the default tracker for a new project. Do NOT rip out beads support — /core:beads remains a legitimate marketplace skill for users whose repos use beads (claude-skills-136 was explicit about this), so beads stays available, e.g. behind a flag, with bees as the default path. title: Subset-aware SATELLITES shape: check what a subsetting tier omits, not just what it names
description: Gate 3 on PR #145 confirmed the subsetting exemption's floor has no teeth. In a scratchpad clone, deleting /core:anti-fabrication from references/validator.md — the one skill that PR's own text calls never-omissible — left both 'nu test/validate-core-list.nu' and 'nu test/validate-skills-quality.nu' at exit 0. The invocations check catches a name that does not RESOLVE (verified: bogus name fails; and simulating removal of ./skills/tdd from plugins/core/.claude-plugin/plugin.json makes every /core:tdd mention fail), so stale and misspelled names cannot survive a core-list change. What is unchecked is MEMBERSHIP: a tier silently dropping a skill it should carry passes CI. That is the exact class that produced claude-skills-125, which was invisible to CI for as long as it existed. Proposed shape: a subset-aware SATELLITES entry {path, expected: [names...]} so validate-core-list.nu asserts a declared subset exactly, rather than requiring the full canonical list or skipping the file. Two files would use it today: references/validator.md (2 names) and references/fix-agent.md (5 names). Deliberately not blocking #145 — the adjacent prose says anti-fabrication is never omissible, so a silent drop requires editing past an explicit warning, and the accidental case is now a documented decision instead.

title: Self-test the duplicate-block count accumulation directly
description: Gate 3 on PR #144 found one mutation the 14 new self-tests do not catch: removing the failing_counts append in Pass 3 leaves both 'nu test/validate-skills-quality.nu --self-test' (14/14) and the full run green. Nothing pins that main actually feeds window counts into the ratchet, which is the absorption trap the validator warns about at its own line ~1010. Behaviour is correct today — verified live in a scratchpad clone: growing the waived beads/bees group 7->8 windows exits 1 with 'current 8 > baselined 7', and shrinking it to 3 exits 1 on stale count, with --update-baseline correctly ratcheting the entry down. The gap is architectural and shared with every pre-existing detail check, since counts are accumulated inline in main rather than in a testable function; it is NOT a regression introduced by #144. Fix: extract the {key, count} accumulation into a function and self-test it directly, which would cover the existing detail checks at the same time. Second, smaller item from the same review: exemption 3 parses validate-core-list.nu with a regex matching 'path: "' anywhere in the file, and self-test case 14 asserts only a lower bound (>=5 satellites). A future 'path: "' string in that script — a test fixture, say — would silently broaden the exemption. Bound the parse to the SATELLITES block and add an upper-bound assertion.

comments.text:
Third instance of the same root cause, from Gate 3 on PR #148 — main's wiring is not unit-testable, so any single-line caller in main can be deleted with every self-test green.

Instances so far: (1) removing the failing_counts append in Pass 3 leaves 15 cases green (the original report); (2) unwiring the floor check from main leaves all vocab cases green (Gate 3 on #147, judged inherent); (3) deleting the skip-warning print line in the corpus scan produces zero skip lines and nothing fails (Gate 3 on #148). In #148 the warning CONTENT was moved into split-corpus-paths so a self-test pins it — the mutation 'helper returns no warnings' is now caught — but the one-line 'for w in ... print' caller in main remains unprotected.

The pattern: extracting the VALUE into a pure helper makes the value testable; it does not make the WIRING testable. Every pass has this shape.

Fix shape, unchanged: an integration harness that runs main against a small fixture repo and asserts on its output, rather than more per-value extraction. That would cover all three instances at once. Judged disproportionate at each individual finding; recording the third instance because the count is the argument — if a fourth shows up, the harness is cheaper than continuing to argue it down case by case.

title: dedupe cross-skill duplicate blocks flagged by duplicate_block check
description: Burn-down for five cross-file duplicate groups baselined when the duplicate-block check landed (claude-skills-124). Groups (key — shared 8-line windows — members): dupe/1182fd06 — 5 — elixir phoenix/references/tidewave.md vs tidewave/SKILL.md; dupe/abe3453c — 2 — claude-code claude-plugins/SKILL.md vs plugin-marketplace/SKILL.md; dupe/da5499df — 2 — claude-plugins/SKILL.md vs plugin-marketplace/references/schema-specification.md; dupe/ccc3a496 — 7 — root CLAUDE.md vs claude-code claude-skills/SKILL.md; dupe/639413bb — 1 — github dependabot-consolidator/references/registration.md vs pr-review/references/registration.md. Run nu test/validate-skills-quality.nu to see current members/counts.

title: dedupe beads-worker/bees-worker shared git/PR block via skills: preloading assessment
description: Duplicate-block check group dupe/6365464e (7 shared windows) spans plugins/core/skills/beads/agents/beads-worker.md and plugins/core/skills/bees/agents/bees-worker.md. Corrected constraint from the claude-skills-124 plan (revision 2), quoted verbatim — do not act on the earlier false categorical version ('pointers do not work; both agents must carry the full workflow'): 'a markdown citation is not followed at spawn time, so the pointer shape used for references does not transfer; `skills:` preloading is the candidate mechanism. Two open questions for whoever takes it — whether preloading `/core:git` (220 lines) to remove ~21 duplicated lines is a favourable trade for an agent whose value is a tight prompt, and how to parameterise the `bd` vs `bees` commands that interleave with the shared block.' title: rust-implementer's Gate 1/Gate 2 collide with the merge-policy gate numbers
description:
plugins/languages/rust/agents/rust-implementer.md:37-38 uses 'Gate 1 — frozen tests untouched' and 'Gate 2 — full CI green' as its own step names. Since PR #143 those numbers collide with /core:git's Three-Gate Merge Policy, where Gate 1 is local CI and Gate 2 is remote CI — so rust's 'Gate 2' is the policy's Gate 1.

Behaviour is unambiguous today: each rust step names its criterion inline and never cites /core:git's numbering, and Gate 3 review judged the non-change defensible. But two schemes sharing the word 'Gate' with different numbers is the kind of thing that reads fine to the author and confuses everyone else.

Cheap fix: rename rust's to 'Check 1 — frozen tests untouched' and 'Check 2 — full CI green', or fold them into the numbered list without gate language. Verify no other agent or skill cites rust's numbering before renaming.

Raised by the Gate 3 review of PR #143 as a non-blocking follow-up.

title: Judgment-over-rules pass on the densest prescriptive skills
description:
Deferred from claude-skills-123, which reconciled the cap literals and applied rule 4 to the authoring skills. This is the other half: apply the judgment-over-rules practice to the skills carrying the most prohibition-shaped prose.

Bounded by a measured selection rule rather than 'the densest ones'. Prohibition-keyword density (grep -cEi 'never|do not|don.t|must not|no exceptions') ranks:
  agent-loop 19, twelve-factor 13, claude-agents 9, restraint 9, git 9

Apply the boundary test from plugins/tools/claude-code/skills/claude-skills/references/context-engineering-claude-5.md to EACH rule individually, not to the file: if removing the prescription would break a check, permit a fabrication, or rely on an agent recognising a need it does not yet have, it stays prescriptive.

Expect this to be small. The top two are exactly the skills that reference's boundary section protects as push-not-pull standing disciplines — agent-loop carries the mandatory-load doctrine and twelve-factor is mandatory precisely because its Use when trigger under-fires. Most of their prohibitions are likely facts. That is a finding to record, not a reason to skip the pass.

Do NOT soften anything backed by a validator check, mise test:disclosure, or the CI gates. Re-measure the density ranking before starting; it will have shifted.

title: Six skills have sibling reference-to-reference links
description:
The ref_depth waivers that are genuine DEBT rather than check defects. Each is a reference file linking to a sibling reference in the same skill, which breaks the one-level-deep rule (SKILL.md to reference, never reference to reference) — an agent following the chain pays for two loads when the body should have pointed at both.

Six entries carrying nine findings:
- awman/awman (2): workflows.md, command-reference.md, api.md cross-link each other
- core/git (2): two sibling cross-links
- qa/qa (2): stack-detection.md and gherkin-format.md link each other
- claude-code/claude-teams (1): references/subagents.md:144 links sibling agent-sdk.md
- elixir/testing (1): tdd-discipline.md links os-subprocess-adapter.md
- slidev/styles (1): discovery-pipeline.md links theme-generation.md

Fix per link: either promote the pointer into the SKILL.md body so both references are reachable at one level, or merge the two references if the split was arbitrary. Reword rather than delete — the cross-reference exists because a reader needs both.

Filed by claude-skills-130's review: these waivers pointed at claude-skills-134 (Harden core-list check), which mentions ref_depth zero times. Second instance of pointer rot found since the class/issue requirement landed in PR #137 — that requirement catches a MISSING pointer, not a wrong one.

title: 14 non-always-loaded skills exceed the 500-line cap
description:
The lines waivers remaining after claude-skills-121 split the always-loaded ones (mise, nushell, twelve-factor). These 14 are over the cap but are NOT in the mandatory core set, so their bodies load only on activation and the cost is bounded:

core/beads 735, core/bees 581, core/code-review 611, core/container 793, core/documentation 676, dagu/workflows 833, elixir/anti-patterns 589, elixir/config 616, elixir/otp 719, elixir/phoenix 599, elixir/style 514, elixir/testing 853, github/act 653, github/workflows 887.

Line counts as of 2026-07-26; re-measure before acting. Same treatment as claude-skills-121: move detail into references/ (one level deep, every file linked from SKILL.md), keep the decision-shaped content and gotchas in the body, then let the ratchet's stale-count rule force each waiver's detail_count down or its removal.

Note core/bees at 581 is the closest to the cap and is a tracker skill agents load constantly — likely the highest value of the group despite not being mandatory.

Split out of claude-skills-121 (closed) so these waivers point at live work, per the class/issue requirement from claude-skills-132.
close_reason: All 14 skills under the 500-line cap across four batches; PRs 152, 156, 157, 158, 159. Zero :lines keys remain in the baseline; waivers 95 to 68. Final sweep: no SKILL.md exceeds 500 lines repo-wide.

comments.text:
PREMISE CORRECTION, found by plan review before any edit. This issue's description says the 14 'are NOT in the mandatory core set, so their bodies load only on activation and the cost is bounded.' That is FALSE for core/bees: /core:bees is item 10 of the canonical mandatory block in agent-loop/SKILL.md, so it loads on EVERY agent at EVERY tier — the same cost profile as the mise/nushell/twelve-factor cohort that claude-skills-121 split. Its 581 lines are paid on every spawn.

The other 13 genuinely are activation-only; the error is bees-specific. Consequence: bees deserves the LEAST conservative trim of the group, not the most, and any batch decision that leans on 'bounded cost' must exclude it.

Also recorded for the batch that follows — plan review measured which mechanics do NOT generalise from the bees slice:
- 7 of the 13 have no usable references/ dir (core/documentation, elixir/anti-patterns, elixir/config, elixir/otp, elixir/style, github/act, github/workflows; dagu/workflows' dir is empty). They need directory + orphan-link plumbing that bees did not.
- github/workflows (887, 387 over), elixir/testing (853), dagu/workflows (833) will need multiple reference files and likely body condensation closer to #121's more aggressive treatment. The bees slice's 'move, not trim, account for every line' constraint is BEES-SPECIFIC and should not be inherited as part of the rule.
- elixir/style (514, 14 over) is the opposite edge: apply the principle, and resist moving more than the lookup content just to reach a rounder number.

Coordination risk: core/bees:anti_fab is waived under claude-skills-144. If 144 edits bees SKILL.md, these line counts drift — re-measure bees at execution time.

FIRST SLICE SHIPPED — PR #150. core/bees 581 -> 356 lines, waivers 82 -> 81. Thirteen skills remain.

THE RULE, validated by contact and safe to inherit: the body answers 'should I, and what will bite me'; references answer 'how exactly'. A section stays if it is a decision, a gotcha, or the happy path; it moves if a reader would look it up rather than read it through. Gate 3 read the 356-line result cold and found nothing missing that you would need before opening a reference, and nothing left in the body that is pure lookup.

SIX MECHANICS NOTES FOR THE BATCH, five sound and one rewritten:
1. Classify SUBSECTIONS, not H2s. This slice moved three subsections out of parents that stayed — that is what let gotchas remain while lookup left.
2. 'Happy path' means the PROCEDURAL happy path. A workflow an agent adapts in-conversation stays; a script artifact you open to copy moves.
3. Keep each moved section's heading as a pointer anchor. MANDATORY where external citations exist — pm and qa sources.md cite bees/SKILL.md, and the anchors keep those resolving. Grep for citations before removing a heading.
4. Deliberate body/reference duplication is sometimes right (the dep-order gotcha lives in both). Cap it at single lines — never blocks, or the duplicate_block check fires.
5. REWRITTEN, and this is the highest-value lesson: byte-faithful moving plus a correction manufactures same-file contradictions. WHEN YOU CORRECT A CLAIM, GREP THE BODY AND EVERY REFERENCE FOR RESTATEMENTS BEFORE COMMITTING. This slice proved it twice — the corrected create examples left a flags list six lines below still documenting the removed flags, and a grep afterwards found the same broken flag in teams-integration.md, a file the PR never touched.
6. A 2-line install stub plus a template pointer is enough to actually install. Fine as the batch default.

DO NOT INHERIT: the 'account for every line' constraint was bees-specific. github/workflows is 387 over and needs real condensation; accounting for every line would block it.

UNEXPECTED FINDING WORTH EXPECTING AGAIN: this trim turned into a correctness fix. The bees Commands Reference documented four things the binary does not do (update --labels, create -l, create -p as parent, comma-separated labels) and the body claimed cycle detection that does not exist — bees 0.4.0 accepts a 2-cycle at exit 0 and both issues then vanish from bees ready. Budget for the possibility that moving content surfaces wrong content, and decide in advance whether to fix in-slice or file. Filed here: claude-skills-157 (audit the rest of commands.md against the binary) and claude-skills-158 (the mise.toml template forwards the broken flags).

REMAINING 13, re-measure before starting: github/workflows 887, elixir/testing 853, dagu/workflows 833, core/container 793, core/beads 735, elixir/otp 719, core/documentation 676, github/act 653, elixir/config 616, core/code-review 611, elixir/phoenix 599, elixir/anti-patterns 589, elixir/style 514. Seven have no usable references/ dir.

BATCH 2 of 4 SHIPPED — PR #152, github plugin. workflows 887 -> 210, act 653 -> 454. Waivers 81 -> 79. Eleven skills remain.

THE RULE HELD AT THE HARDEST CASE. workflows was the largest gap in the program (387 over) and the bees plan review predicted it would need body condensation beyond the move-only approach. It did not: 631 of its 887 lines were contiguous GitHub Actions YAML syntax reference, which is look-it-up content by definition, so a straight move handled it. Gate 3 read the resulting 210-line body cold as an author and found nothing missing before opening a reference. A 76% cut was a trim, not an evisceration, because the thing being cut was uniformly one kind of content.

FOUR MECHANICS FOR BATCHES 3 AND 4, all Gate-3 assessed as sound:
1. Name a destination file for EVERY moved item in the plan. Revision 2 left two moved patterns without a target and the implementer had to choose.
2. Budget ~4 lines per moved H2 for pointer anchors before promising a body size. 13 anchors cost ~50 lines here and put the result 10 over target.
3. Scan same-file windows BY HAND after a wholesale move. The duplicate_block check windows are CROSS-FILE only, so two overlapping sections landing in one reference file are invisible to CI. One instance was caught and fixed by hand this batch.
4. Body/reference near-duplication is fine where the two versions genuinely carry different things (a worked example including an invocation the raw payload lacks). Not a violation of the single-line duplication cap.

THIRD SLICE, THIRD TIME A TRIM SURFACED FALSE CONTENT — treat this as expected, not surprising. act documented three things that do not work, all verified against act 0.2.89: 'act --shell bash' (no such flag, zero occurrences in --help), 'if: github.event_name != \\'act\\'' (act passes the real event name; there is no act event, so the guard never fires and the local-only step never runs — found in THREE places, not the two the plan named), and '--container-daemon-socket -' described as host networking (it is the Docker socket URI; --network already defaults to host). Budget for this in batches 3 and 4.

ONE SCOPE DECISION WORTH INHERITING: every GitHub Action pin in the workflows skill is 2-4 majors stale (checkout v4 vs v7.0.1). NOT fixed here, deliberately — pins appear in both moving and kept sections, so a partial bump manufactures the body/reference contradiction that bit #150. Bump all or none; this bumped none, leaving the skill uniformly stale, which is self-consistent and wrong in one way rather than two. Filed as claude-skills-161 covering the skill, its new references, and our own validate.yml.

REMAINING 11, re-measure before starting: elixir/testing 853, dagu/workflows 833, core/container 793, core/beads 735, elixir/otp 719, core/documentation 676, elixir/config 616, core/code-review 611, elixir/phoenix 599, elixir/anti-patterns 589, elixir/style 514. Suggested next batch: core (4 skills), then elixir (6), then dagu (1).

title: Decide the name_dir convention: plugin-prefixed frontmatter name vs bare directory name
description:
19 of the 125 quality-baseline waivers are name_dir — the largest single group after anti_fab. All 19 are the same deliberate pattern: frontmatter uses a <plugin>-<skill> prefix (dagu-rest-api, github-workflows, slidev-*, zig-*) while the directory is the bare name, and the check requires name to match the directory exactly.

This needs ONE decision, then it is mechanical either way:
(a) Keep the prefixed frontmatter names and relax the check to accept <plugin>-<dir>, or
(b) Drop the prefixes so name matches the directory, per the Agent Skills spec rule this repo states ('Must exactly match the name property').

Note the interaction with command naming: for PLUGIN skills the frontmatter name sets the last segment of the invocation, so dropping a prefix changes how the skill is invoked. Verify that before choosing (b).

Needed by claude-skills-132, which requires every waiver to carry a linked issue — these 19 entries point here.
close_reason:
Shipped as PR #149. Option (b): dropped the <plugin>- prefixes from 19 skill frontmatter names so name matches the directory. Waivers 101 -> 82, the largest single reduction of this run; zero name_dir remaining, source unchanged at 8.

THE DECISION'S BLOCKER DID NOT EXIST. The issue hedged on whether the frontmatter name sets the invocation segment. It does not — invocation is directory-driven, verified three times independently: zig/skills/build had 'name: zig-build' and lists as 'zig:build'; the validator registry is built from plugin.json skill PATHS (line 1496); upstream docs describe name as a display field defaulting to the directory. Option (a) — relax the check — was rejected as weakening a spec check to accommodate redundant prefixes.

THIS FINISHED A MIGRATION RATHER THAN STARTING ONE. Closed issue claude-skills-90 records PRs #111/#112 doing the same rename for elixir; rust/testing, rust/troubleshooting and elixir/testing already carried bare names on main, so cross-plugin bare duplicates were already live and harmless.

MY CATALOG DESIGN WAS WRONG AND REVIEW REVERSED IT. I proposed converting README and skill-catalog entries to the invocation form (slidev:code) on the reasoning that bare names are ambiguous 'in a flat catalog'. The catalogs are not flat — they are sectioned by plugin, and every other section already used bare names (README:115-117 dagu, :135-138 github; skill-catalog's elixir and github rows). Invocation form would have introduced a third style. Reasoning confidently from an unchecked premise, same shape as generalising N=3 to N=8 in claude-skills-124.

FOUR TRAPS, ALL AVOIDED: slidev-exported (the exportFilename config default, where slidev-export is a PREFIX of it); a #slidev-export-configuration TOC anchor whose heading would go stale; four real docs.github.com/...-github-actions URLs — meaning github, zig and dagu sources.md needed ZERO edits, where my first plan said all per-plugin sources files needed updating; and .bees/issues.jsonl tracker history, left untouched. Gate 3 confirmed all three trap files byte-identical to main.

One plan claim was wrong and is corrected on the record: bees skill: labels are plugin-qualified (skill:claude-code:claude-workflows), not bare. The conclusion held anyway — workers consume labels via jq and use the catalog only as a sectioned keyword fallback, so nothing emits labels from catalog rows.

Follow-up filed: claude-skills-156 (sources.md Version lines stale repo-wide against plugin.json; prefers deleting the second copy over building a check to keep two copies equal).

comments.text: BLOCKER RESOLVED, evidence for whoever takes this. The issue asked to verify whether dropping the prefix changes invocation before choosing (b). It does not — invocation is DIRECTORY-driven, not frontmatter-name-driven. Measured: plugins/languages/zig/skills/build has frontmatter 'name: zig-build' and the live skill listing shows it as 'zig:build'; plugins/tools/github/skills/workflows has 'name: github-workflows' and lists as 'github:workflows'; plugins/tools/dagu/skills/rest-api has 'name: dagu-rest-api'. In every case the invocation segment matches the DIRECTORY, not the prefixed frontmatter name. So option (b) — drop the prefixes so name matches the directory — is safe and does not change how any skill is invoked. Recommendation: take (b). It deletes 19 waivers, matches the Agent Skills spec rule this repo already states ('Must exactly match the name property'), and avoids option (a)'s cost of weakening a spec check to accommodate redundant prefixes. Still needs an operator decision, but the risk that motivated the hedge is measured and absent.

title: Remove dead beads tooling: 6 tracked files, a post-merge hook, and an untracked dolt dir
description:
This repo's CLAUDE.md states bees is the tracker and 'beads is removed from all repos', but beads is still wired in and firing on every merge.

Evidence:
- 6 tracked files under .beads/: .gitignore, README.md, config.yaml, interactions.jsonl, issues.jsonl, metadata.json.
- .beads/issues.jsonl holds 9 issues, latest activity 2026-02-21. The live tracker .bees/issues.jsonl holds 135.
- .git/hooks/post-merge is a beads hook that runs 'bd import' after every pull or merge. It printed 'Failed to import bd changes after merge' when PR #131 was squash-merged.
- An untracked .beads/embeddeddolt/ directory keeps reappearing in git status and has been noise in every status check this session.

Proposed cleanup, needs an operator decision because it deletes tracked data:
1. Confirm the 9 beads issues are genuinely dead or migrate anything still wanted into bees.
2. git rm -r .beads/ and remove the post-merge hook.
3. Add .beads/ to .gitignore so a stray local beads install cannot re-add it.

Do NOT do step 2 before step 1 — the file is tracked issue history, and deleting it is irreversible from the working tree alone.

Note /core:beads remains a legitimate SKILL in the marketplace for users whose repos use beads; this issue is only about this repo's own dead installation, not the skill.

Shipped as PR #146. Removed this repo's dead beads installation: .beads/ (6 tracked files + the untracked embeddeddolt dir), the .git/hooks/post-merge import hook, .gitattributes (deleted outright — its only content was the merge=beads driver, and bees uses none), and 221 lines from mise.toml (the beads tool install + all 20 beads:* tasks, an operator-approved scope extension since mise install was still pulling the binary). .beads/ added to .gitignore. 432 deletions, 10 insertions.

/core:beads is UNTOUCHED and remains in the marketplace. It does not depend on this repo's mise tasks — it tells users to add their own (beads/SKILL.md:53). This removed an installation, not a skill.

STEP 1 MATTERED AND I GOT IT HALF RIGHT. Of the 9 tracked issues, 8 were closed (outcomes spot-checked as shipped) and 1 was open: a P2 typescript plugin spec with no such plugin in the marketplace and nothing in bees covering it. Migrated to claude-skills-153 before deleting. But the migration copied only the DESCRIPTION — Gate 3 found the record also carried 2 comments and 4 labels, and both comments were titled CORRECTION and superseded the description (correct path is plugins/languages/typescript/, and the structure is 6 skills using the references pattern, not 4). An agent picking up 153 as first migrated would have built the wrong thing at the wrong path. Recovered verbatim from git history and re-added with provenance headers. Recoverable only because the data was still one commit back.

Documentation the change obligated: this repo's own PR workflow instructed bd close / git add .beads/ / bd ready — dead instructions, updated to bees. Two commit/PR format examples held up 'add beads tooling to mise.toml' as the model change. And AGENTS.md still told non-Claude harnesses 'This project uses bd (beads)... run bd onboard' — found by Gate 3, not by my sweep, because I grepped for the .beads DIRECTORY rather than the bd TOOL. Converted to a symlink to CLAUDE.md per the workspace convention, which is what stops it drifting again.

title: Harden core-list check: remaining follow-ups from PR #131 review
description:
Non-blocking hardening identified by the fable review of PR #131. The check is correct on the current corpus and negative-tested in both drift directions; these are edge cases that all fail LOUD rather than passing silently, which is why they were not blockers.

1. Fence info-string parsing: a fence opened as triple-backtick immediately followed by a skill name parses as a G1 names-only line, because backtick stripping runs before tokenising. Contrived (no current file does this) but the fix is to skip fence-delimiter lines explicitly before applying G1.

2. EXCLUDED_PARTIAL is documentation shaped as executable config: the const at test/validate-core-list.nu:71-74 is never referenced by code — exclusion is actually implicit in the SATELLITES allowlist. Wiring it buys nothing today, since validator.md's inline numbered form parses under neither grammar. Either annotate it 'documentation only — not referenced by code' or demote it to a comment block. Currently it implies enforcement that does not exist.

3. G1 strips a trailing comma but not a trailing period, while G2 strips both. A names-only line ending in a period fails G1. Safe direction (reports drift rather than passing), but the asymmetry is arbitrary — make both strip the same trailing punctuation set.

Already fixed pre-merge, recorded here so the reasoning is not lost: G2 now requires the remainder after the skill name to be empty or start with an open paren, so a prose bullet like '- /core:tdd — standing discipline' is no longer counted as a load-list entry. Without that, such a bullet could MASK a genuinely missing name, which is the same false-pass class the structural check was built to remove. Verified with a masking test: name removed from work.md's real list plus present as a prose bullet fails correctly. Also unified the canonical extractor and both grammars onto shared CORE_NAME and SKILL_NAME consts; they previously disagreed on case and digits, so /core:s3-tools would parse in a satellite but drop from the canonical block.
close_reason: Closed with PR #139 (a598efe): fence delimiters explicitly excluded from the grammar via a shared is-fence-delimiter predicate, EXCLUDED_PARTIAL demoted from documentation-shaped-as-config to a header comment naming claude-skills-125, and the G1/G2 punctuation asymmetry dissolved with G2's deletion.

comments.text:
CORRECTION to this issue's framing, and one item removed because it was fixed.

My original text said the remaining edges 'all fail LOUD rather than passing silently'. That was FALSE. An adversarial review found two SILENT false passes in the same class, both tool-verified by me independently:

- PoC A: with /core:tdd deleted from work.md's real list, appending '- `/core:tdd` (standing discipline)' anywhere in the file made the check print a green tick for that file.
- PoC B: same deletion, plus a fenced worked example containing bare /core:tdd on its own line. Also green.

Root cause: extract-load-list-names unioned every G1/G2 hit across the whole file and compared sets per FILE rather than per LIST, so any second occurrence anywhere restored a deleted name to the union. My earlier pre-merge G2 fix (requiring a paren rather than an em-dash after the name) closed ONE idiom and simultaneously blessed the more dangerous one — it documented paren-annotated bullets as legitimate list entries with nothing keeping authors from using that idiom in prose.

FIXED in PR #131 rather than deferred here, since a silent false pass in a check people trust is worse than a stale diff: lists are now compared per contiguous RUN of list lines. A run carrying fewer than 2 /core: names is ignored (so a lone prose mention still costs nothing), and more than one qualifying run in a satellite is reported as ambiguous rather than guessed at. Regression matrix now covers five cases — both PoCs FAIL, lone prose bullet PASSES, extra-name-in-list FAILS, missing-name FAILS.

The header comment was also overclaiming ('prose mentions are ignored by design' was untrue for paren bullets; 'both drift directions are checked' was maskable). Rewritten to state what the check guarantees and to list three things it still cannot see.

STILL OPEN in this issue: the fence info-string edge, the trailing-punctuation asymmetry between G1 and G2, and EXCLUDED_PARTIAL being unreferenced documentation shaped like executable config. Those three genuinely do fail loud or are cosmetic.

Refinement after attempting to break the per-run design myself. Three attacks run:

ATTACK 1 — delete a name from its position and re-add it as a paren bullet adjacent to the real list, so it joins the same run: FAILS correctly (the placeholder line splits the run). Note the genuine case — name deleted from position and re-added inside the same contiguous run with no gap — PASSES, and that is correct: the name really is in the list. Recorded in the header as behaviour, not a gap.

ATTACK 2 — blank line inside a single logical list: FAILS. A false fail, accepted because it is loud and names the parsed runs.

ATTACK 3 — a satellite carrying a SECOND complete example list: FAILED under the 'exactly one run' rule. That was a real usability defect, not an edge case: leader-spawn-example.md exists to hold worked examples, so adding a second one would have broken CI for legitimate content.

Fixed by replacing 'exactly one run' with 'EVERY run must match canonical'. Strictly better — both masking PoCs still fail (their partial run disagrees with canonical), while a second correct list now passes. Regression matrix is 7 cases: baseline PASS, PoC A FAIL, PoC B FAIL, lone prose bullet PASS, extra-name FAIL, missing-name FAIL, second-complete-list PASS.

Header comment corrected again — it had been rewritten to describe the single-run rule that no longer exists, and now also records the two accepted false-fail cases (blank-line split, deliberate partial list).

5. Hedging-verb prohibition is stated three times (claude-skills:134, again at :366-376, and plugins/tools/claude-code/hooks/session-start.sh:20-21) with no validator check behind it. Collapse to one judgment line in claude-skills and drop the other two.

title: pm agents still imply bees prime returns issue data
description:
Left as a follow-up by Gate 3 on PR #151 rather than widening a 12-file PR to 14.

plugins/pm/agents/pm-discovery.md:40 and plugins/pm/agents/pm-lead.md:94 list 'bees prime' in the bees-map command surface with wording that implies it contributes issue data — 'List each issue's id, title, status ... as returned by these commands'. PR #151 established and verified that prime returns NO issue data at all: 58 lines of static agent-workflow cheatsheet, zero issue-id mentions in a repo holding four issues. The bees-to-spec.md reference these agents defer to was corrected in #151 and now says so; the agent files were not.

Harmless in practice — prime is read-only and the other commands in the same list (bees list --json, bees show --json) do supply the data, so the shard still gets what it needs. But the wording tells an agent to expect issue data from a command that never returns any, which is the same false-expectation class #151 removed everywhere else.

Fix: drop 'bees prime' from the 'as returned by these commands' enumeration in both files, or move it to a separate line noting it returns workflow context rather than issues. Two one-line edits plus a pm version bump.
